definition_zh: 月；月份；一个月的时间；漫长的岁月（复数）
definition_en: one of the twelve divisions of the year, also a period of about thirty days and, in the plural, a long stretch of time
core_image: 日历上撕下的一页，边缘还留着月亮的弧度
scene: 月底的夜里，桌上的账单摊开，日期一格一格逼近。The rent falls due at the start of every month.
sceneCN: 这里是「月份、月」（第 1 个义项：日历上的一年十二分之一）；句意为每到月初房租就到期。图中可辨识物件：账单、日历、台灯。

pos.zh: 月；月份；一个月的时间；漫长的岁月

derivatives.zh: 由 month 加 -ly 构成，义为「每月的；每月一次」
由 month 与 long 复合而成，义为「持续一个月的」
由前缀 bi-（两个）加 monthly 构成，义为「两月一次的」

senses.title: One of the twelve divisions of the year
senses.definition: one of the twelve named divisions of the calendar year
senses.definitionCN: 日历年里十二个有名称的划分之一
senses.example: February is the shortest month of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 二月是一年里最短的月份。
senses.why: A month began as the moon's own cycle, so the word for the unit still carries the shape of a turning moon.
senses.whyCN: 月份最初就是月亮自己的一轮周期，所以这个表单位的词里仍留着月亮转动的形状。

senses.title: A period of about thirty days
senses.definition: a span of roughly thirty days used as a unit of time
senses.definitionCN: 用作计时单位的大约三十天的一段时间
senses.example: The repairs took a month to finish.
senses.exampleCN: 修理工作花了一个月才完成。
senses.why: Once the unit is fixed, it can measure any span of about thirty days, whether or not the calendar page matches.
senses.whyCN: 单位一旦固定，它就能用来量任何约三十天的时间段，不必与日历那一页严格对齐。

senses.title: A long stretch of time, in the plural
senses.definition: a long time, used in the plural to suggest a slow wait
senses.definitionCN: 很长的一段时间，用复数来表示漫长的等待
senses.example: She has not written to us for months.
senses.exampleCN: 她好几个月没有给我们写信了。
senses.why: Counting months is slow, so a plural pile of them naturally stands for a long wait.
senses.whyCN: 按月计数本来就慢，于是复数的月份自然就表示一段漫长的等待。

senses.title: The lunar cycle
senses.definition: the period from one new moon to the next, about twenty-nine and a half days
senses.definitionCN: 从一个新月到下一个新月的周期，约二十九天半
senses.example: A lunar month lasts about twenty-nine and a half days.
senses.exampleCN: 一个太阴月约持续二十九天半。
senses.why: The moon-based origin keeps a technical sense alive in astronomy, where a lunar month runs from one new moon to the next.
senses.whyCN: 以月亮为起点的来源让一个术语义在天文学里保留下来：太阴月从一个新月走到下一个新月。

intro.en: The English month is a Germanic word built on the moon, and its oldest sense is a moon-driven cycle rather than a page on a wall.
intro.cn: 英语的 month 是建立在月亮之上的日耳曼词，它最早的意思是被月亮推动的一轮周期，而不是墙上的一页纸。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to measure is generally thought to lie behind the words for moon and month in both the Germanic and the Latin branches.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个表示「测量」的印欧语重构词根同时藏在日耳曼语和拉丁语中表示月亮与月份的词后面。

items.en: Old English mōnaþ joined mōna, the moon, with the noun suffix -þ, so the month was literally the moon's turning.
items.cn: 古英语 mōnaþ 把 mōna（月亮）与名词后缀 -þ 结合，所以月份字面上就是月亮的一轮转动。

items.en: Related forms such as Old Frisian mōnath and German Monat show the same moon-based naming across the Germanic languages.
items.cn: 古弗里斯兰语的 mōnath、德语的 Monat 等相关形式显示，日耳曼各语言都用月亮来命名月份。

items.en: Middle English moneth kept the moon inside the word while the spelling slowly moved toward the modern month.
items.cn: 中古英语的 moneth 仍把月亮留在词里，拼写则慢慢向现代形式 month 靠拢。

items.en: Modern English month covers the calendar unit, the lunar cycle and, in the plural, a long stretch of time.
items.cn: 现代英语的 month 兼指日历单位、月相周期，复数还表示很长一段时间。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the same moon stem, while the near-meaning group collects the other units used to count time.
note.cn: 形近组收同一月亮词干上的形式，近义组收用来计时的其他单位。

entries.definition: Happening once every month or issued each month.
entries.definitionCN: 由 month 加 -ly 构成，义为「每月的；每月一次」。

entries.definition: The body whose cycle gave the month its name.
entries.definitionCN: 其周期为月份提供名称的天体，月亮。

entries.definition: The day named after the moon, from the same Old English stem.
entries.definitionCN: 以月亮命名的日子，来自同一个古英语词干。

entries.definition: A period of seven days, the unit just below a month.
entries.definitionCN: 七天的一段时间，是比月更小的计时单位。

entries.definition: A period of twelve months.
entries.definitionCN: 十二个月的一段时间。

entries.definition: A period of two weeks, common in British usage.
entries.definitionCN: 两周的一段时间，英式用法中常见。

entries.definition: A period of twenty-four hours.
entries.definitionCN: 二十四小时的一段时间。

normalIntro.en: The word is a moon-word from start to finish, and its family keeps returning to cycling light and counted time.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从头到尾都是月亮词，它的同族词也一直回到光的循环与被数出来的时间。

normal.en: Old English mōnaþ is moon plus a noun ending, so the month was named after the moon that paced it.
normal.cn: 古英语 mōnaþ 是月亮加一个名词词尾，月份是用给它定节奏的月亮命名的。

normal.en: German Monat and Dutch maand keep the same m-n shape, which is why the English word looks so plain.
normal.cn: 德语 Monat 与荷兰语 maand 保留同样的 m-n 骨架，所以英语这个词显得格外朴素。

normal.en: monthly adds -ly to month: something that happens once in each month.
normal.cn: monthly 在 month 后加 -ly，表示在每个月发生一次的事物。

normal.en: The plural months often means a long time, as in letters unanswered for months.
normal.cn: 复数的 months 常表示很久，例如好几个月没有回信。

normal.en: Latin mensis is a distant cousin rather than a borrowing, which is why English did not take a Latin shape.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mensis 是远亲而不是借词，所以英语没有采用拉丁语的词形。

abstract.en: A calendar is a row of moons, each one handing its name to a page.
abstract.cn: 日历就是一排月亮，每一个把自己的名字交给一页纸。

abstract.en: Turn a page and a moon has already happened.
abstract.cn: 翻过一页，就有一轮月亮已经走完。

abstract.en: The word is older than paper: people counted months by looking up.
abstract.cn: 这个词比纸更老：人们曾靠抬头看天来数月份。

examples.en: February is the shortest month of the year.
examples.cn: 二月是一年里最短的月份。

examples.en: The repairs took a month to finish.
examples.cn: 修理工作花了一个月才完成。

examples.en: She has not written to us for months.
examples.cn: 她好几个月没有给我们写信了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「忙死」——月底事情多到忙死；记住 month 就是月。

root: 古英语 mōnaþ 由 mōna（月亮）加名词后缀 -þ 构成，本义是月亮的一轮；一般认为它与拉丁语 mensis 同出印欧语表示「测量」的词根。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the calendar unit, and the senses then branch into a measured span, a slow plural of waiting, and the lunar cycle underneath it all.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是日历上的月份；义项由此分出被丈量的时间段、表示漫长等待的复数，以及藏在底下的月相周期。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a page torn from a calendar, its edge still curved like a moon.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张从日历上撕下的纸，边缘仍带着月牙的弧度。

branches.en: a calendar page torn off on the first day
branches.cn: 月初撕下的一页日历

branches.en: a repair job stretching across thirty days
branches.cn: 一项横跨三十天的修理活

branches.en: letters left unanswered for a season
branches.cn: 一整个季节无人回的信

branches.en: a chart tracing new moon to new moon
branches.cn: 从新月画到新月的图

branches.en: rent falling due as a month turns
branches.cn: 月份交替时到期的房租

intro.en: The word is held together by a moon noun, an old noun ending, and the two suffixes that turn it into a monthly adjective.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示月亮的名词、一个古老的名词词尾，以及把它变成「每月的」形容词的两个后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin mensis and menstruus belong to the same distant Indo-European family, though English borrowed nothing directly from them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mensis 与 menstruus 属于同一遥远的印欧语族，但英语并没有直接借用它们。

items.meaningCN: 构成形容词与副词的后缀

items.meaning: the body that paces the month

items.meaningCN: 由 moon 与 day 复合

definition_zh: 纪念碑；纪念物；古迹；有永久价值的成就或证据
definition_en: a structure built to commemorate a person or event; a historic site; a lasting example or achievement
core_image: 广场中央的石柱在夕阳下投出长影，碑座上刻着几行名字
scene: 广场中央的石柱在夕阳下投出长影。The monument honors the engineers who built the first bridge.
sceneCN: 这里 monument 指「为纪念人物或事件而建的纪念性建筑」（第 1 个义项：纪念建筑）；句意为这座纪念碑向建造第一座桥的工程师致敬；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 纪念碑；纪念物；古迹；典范；不朽成就

collocations.zh: 国家纪念碑；国家保护区

derivatives.zh: monument + -al（形容词后缀）→ 纪念碑的；巨大的
monumental + -ity（性质后缀）→ 纪念性；宏伟感
monumental + -ly（副词后缀）→ 巨大地；极其
monumental + -ize（动词后缀）→ 使成为纪念物
monumentalize + -ation（名词后缀）→ 纪念化

senses.title: A commemorative structure
senses.definition: a building, statue or stone erected to keep the memory of a person or event
senses.definitionCN: 为保存对某人或某事的记忆而建成的建筑、雕像或石碑
senses.example: The monument honors the engineers who built the first bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 这座纪念碑向建造第一座桥的工程师致敬。
senses.why: monumentum came from monere 'to remind'; the structure exists to make people remember.
senses.whyCN: monumentum 来自 monere「提醒」；这座建筑存在的目的就是让人记住。

senses.title: A historic building or site
senses.definition: an old building, ruin or place preserved because of its historical importance
senses.definitionCN: 因历史重要性而被保存的古老建筑、废墟或地点
senses.example: The abbey is listed as a monument of national importance.
senses.exampleCN: 这座修道院被列为具有国家重要性的历史建筑。
senses.why: the same word moved from a purpose-built memorial to any old structure that a nation decides to protect.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词从专门建造的纪念物，扩展到国家决定保护的任何古老建筑。

senses.title: A tombstone or grave memorial
senses.definition: a stone or structure marking a grave and preserving a name
senses.definitionCN: 标记墓地并保存姓名的石碑或建筑
senses.example: A simple monument marks the grave of the village teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 一块朴素的墓碑标出乡村教师的墓。
senses.why: a grave marker is the smallest and oldest kind of memorial, a stone that keeps one name in place.
senses.whyCN: 墓碑是最小、最古老的纪念物，一块石头把一个人的名字留在原处。

senses.title: A lasting evidence or example
senses.definition: something that stands as clear evidence of a quality, often a bad one
senses.definitionCN: 作为某种品质（常为负面）的明显证据的事物
senses.example: The empty factory is a monument to poor planning.
senses.exampleCN: 那座空工厂是规划不善的活证据。
senses.why: the commemorative sense turns ironic: a thing can remind people of a failure as well as a hero.
senses.whyCN: 纪念义可转为反讽：事物既能让人记住英雄，也能让人记住失败。

senses.title: An outstanding achievement or work
senses.definition: a work or achievement so important that it deserves to be remembered
senses.definitionCN: 重要到值得被记住的作品或成就
senses.example: The dictionary is a monument of nineteenth-century scholarship.
senses.exampleCN: 这部词典是十九世纪学术的不朽丰碑。
senses.why: what deserves a monument is what a culture wants to keep, so the word extends from stone to achievement.
senses.whyCN: 值得立碑的东西就是文化想留住的东西，因此词义从石头扩展到成就。

senses.title: An ancient ruin
senses.definition: a surviving structure of an earlier civilization, often visited as a heritage site
senses.definitionCN: 早期文明留存下来的建筑，常作为文化遗产参观
senses.example: Tourists walked among the monuments of the old capital.
senses.exampleCN: 游客在旧都的遗迹间行走。
senses.why: once a whole city is old enough, its surviving structures become monuments by age rather than by design.
senses.whyCN: 当整座城市足够古老，留存下来的建筑就凭年代而非设计成为遗迹。

senses.title: A statue
senses.definition: a sculpted figure set up in public to honor a person
senses.definitionCN: 为纪念某人而置于公共空间的雕塑人像
senses.example: A bronze monument of the founder stands in the square.
senses.exampleCN: 广场上立着创始人的铜像。
senses.why: a statue is a monument given a human shape, the memorial impulse turned into a sculpted body.
senses.whyCN: 雕像是一座拥有人形的纪念碑，是纪念冲动变成雕塑身体。

senses.title: A written memorial record
senses.definition: a written account or record kept to preserve someone's memory
senses.definitionCN: 为保存某人记忆而留下的书面记述或记录
senses.example: The chronicle is a monument in words rather than in stone.
senses.exampleCN: 这部编年史是用文字而非石头筑成的纪念碑。
senses.why: a written record performs the same reminding job as a stone, so the word extends to books and chronicles.
senses.whyCN: 书面记录承担与石头相同的提醒功能，因此词义扩展到书籍与编年史。

intro.en: Monument comes from Latin monumentum, 'a memorial, a monument', from monere 'to remind, warn'. The same verb gives monitor and admonish, so the core idea is something that makes you remember.
intro.cn: monument 来自拉丁 monumentum「纪念物、纪念碑」，源于 monere「提醒、警告」。同一动词还衍生 monitor 与 admonish，核心意思是「让人想起的东西」。

items.en: Monere meant 'to remind, warn, advise', the act behind every monument.
items.cn: monere 意为「提醒、警告、劝告」，是每座纪念碑背后的动作。

items.en: Monumentum was 'a thing that reminds', whether a building, a tomb or a written record.
items.cn: monumentum 指「使人想起的东西」，可以是建筑、坟墓或书面记录。

items.en: English borrowed the word first for a memorial structure or tomb.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入这个词，最初指纪念建筑或坟墓。

items.en: Later it covered preserved old buildings and ruins, especially in heritage law.
items.cn: 后来它覆盖受保护的古老建筑与废墟，尤其在遗产法规中。

items.en: The word then extended to achievements and to ironic examples, as in a monument to folly.
items.cn: 再后来扩展到成就与反讽例证，如「愚蠢的纪念碑」。

note.en: Group one holds memorial objects easily confused with a monument; group two holds words for importance and remembrance.
note.cn: 第一组是容易与 monument 混淆的纪念物；第二组是表示重要与纪念的词。

entries.definition: A object or event that keeps a memory; a monument is one kind, usually built and public.
entries.definitionCN: 保存记忆的物件或活动；monument 是其中一种，通常是建成且公开的。

entries.definition: A small object kept as a reminder; it is personal, while a monument is public and large.
entries.definitionCN: 留作提醒的小物件；属私人性质，纪念碑则公开且宏大。

entries.definition: The describing word for a monument or for something huge; the noun is the object itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述纪念碑或巨大事物的形容词；名词指物件本身。

entries.definition: A written reminder or note; it shares the reminder root but names a document, not a structure.
entries.definitionCN: 书面提醒或便条；共享「提醒」词根，但指文件而非建筑。

entries.definition: A carved or cast figure of a person or animal; a monument may be a statue, but may also be a wall or arch.
entries.definitionCN: 人或动物的雕刻或铸造形象；纪念碑可以是雕像，也可能是墙或拱门。

entries.definition: A holy place or structure marking a sacred person or event; the emphasis is religious.
entries.definitionCN: 标记神圣人物或事件的圣地或建筑；侧重宗教。

entries.definition: A easily recognized feature of a place; a monument is built to remember, a landmark may simply be noticed.
entries.definitionCN: 一个地方易被认出的特征；纪念碑为记忆而建，地标只是显眼。

entries.definition: A grave or burial chamber; a monument may mark a tomb but need not contain a body.
entries.definitionCN: 坟墓或墓室；纪念碑可标记坟墓，但不一定葬有遗体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin reminder verb, the real public object and the ironic extension.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁「提醒」动词、真实的公共物件与反讽引申。

normal.en: monere is 'to remind'; a monument is a reminder made of stone.
normal.cn: monere 是「提醒」；纪念碑是用石头做成的提醒。

normal.en: Monitor and admonish come from the same verb.
normal.cn: monitor 与 admonish 同出这个动词。

normal.en: Heritage law uses monument for protected old buildings.
normal.cn: 遗产法规用 monument 指受保护的古老建筑。

normal.en: A monument can be ironic: a monument to bad planning.
normal.cn: 纪念碑可以带反讽：规划不善的纪念碑。

normal.en: A written chronicle can be called a monument in words.
normal.cn: 一部编年史可称为文字筑成的纪念碑。

abstract.en: A monument is a stone that keeps saying a name after the mouth is gone.
abstract.cn: 纪念碑是一块在嘴消失后仍不断念出名字的石头。

abstract.en: It is memory given a body heavy enough to stay put.
abstract.cn: 它是被赋予足够沉重身体、无法轻易移走的记忆。

abstract.en: A bad monument is a culture arguing with its own past.
abstract.cn: 糟糕的纪念碑，是一个文化在与自己的过去争吵。

examples.en: The city erected a monument to the nurses who died in the epidemic.
examples.cn: 这座城市为死于疫病的护士建立了纪念碑。

examples.en: The old bridge is a monument of early engineering.
examples.cn: 这座旧桥是早期工程的不朽之作。

examples.en: The empty tower stands as a monument to failed ambition.
examples.cn: 那座空塔成了野心失败的一座纪念碑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「monu（提醒）+ ment（物）」——让人记住的东西 → 纪念碑

root: 拉丁 monumentum「使人想起的东西」← monere「提醒、警告」+ -mentum（名词后缀）；同源词有 monitor、admonish。英语 monument。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one reminder: a built memorial, a protected site, a grave, a warning example, an achievement, a ruin, a statue and a written record.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个提醒展开：建成的纪念物、受保护遗址、坟墓、警示例证、成就、废墟、雕像与书面记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy stone standing in a square, repeating a name to everyone who passes.
core.cn: 核心意象：广场上一块沉重的石头，向每个经过的人重复一个名字。

branches.en: STONE MEMORY: a public memorial and a grave marker both make a name outlast a life.
branches.cn: 石头记忆：公共纪念碑与墓碑都让名字活得比生命更久。

branches.en: PROTECTED PAST: a listed building and an ancient ruin are the past kept in place.
branches.cn: 受保护的过去：登录建筑与古代废墟都是被留在原地的过去。

branches.en: VALUE JUDGEMENT: an ironic example and a great achievement both measure a culture's memory.
branches.cn: 价值判断：反讽例证与伟大成就都在衡量一个文化的记忆。

branches.en: HUMAN FIGURE: a statue makes the reminder take a body.
branches.cn: 人形：雕像让提醒拥有身体。

branches.en: WRITTEN STONE: a chronicle is a monument made of words instead of rock.
branches.cn: 文字之石：编年史是用文字而非岩石筑成的纪念碑。

intro.en: Monument is a Latin reminder noun, and its family still carries the idea of warning and memory.
intro.cn: monument 是一个拉丁「提醒」名词，其词族仍带着警告与记忆的意思。

latinIntro.en: Latin monere gives monitor, admonish and monumentum; the suffix -mentum turns the act of reminding into a thing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 monere 衍生 monitor、admonish 与 monumentum；后缀 -mentum 把「提醒」的动作变成物件。

definition_zh: 心情；情绪；气氛；语气（语法）；一时的兴致
definition_en: a temporary state of feeling, or the atmosphere of a place or group, or a grammatical category of the verb
core_image: 天气没有变，屋里的人却觉得整间房子忽明忽暗，像云在屋顶上走
scene: 排练到一半，指挥忽然放下手，说今天先到这里，因为整个乐队已经提不起劲。The conductor stopped the rehearsal because the mood in the hall had gone flat.
sceneCN: 这里 mood 指「一群人当下共同的情绪基调」（第 1 个义项：一时的情绪状态）；句意为指挥中止排练，因为大厅里的情绪已经没了劲。图中可辨识物件：放下的指挥棒、松开的谱架、空着的上半场座位；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: A temporary state of feeling
senses.definition: the way a person feels at a particular time, seen as passing rather than fixed
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在某段时间里的感受状态，被视为会过去而非固定
senses.example: The conductor stopped the rehearsal because the mood in the hall had gone flat.
senses.exampleCN: 指挥中止排练，因为大厅里的情绪已经没了劲。
senses.why: the oldest English sense is simply 'mind, disposition', so the word names the weather inside a person rather than their climate.
senses.whyCN: 最早的英语义就是「心境、性情」，因此这个词命名的是人内部的天气，而不是气候。

senses.title: The atmosphere of a place
senses.definition: the feeling that a room, a street or a gathering gives off
senses.definitionCN: 一间屋子、一条街或一场聚会所散发出的感受
senses.example: Candles on the tables changed the mood of the whole restaurant.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上的蜡烛改变了整间餐馆的气氛。
senses.why: the same word moves from one head to a space, because a space is read as having a temper of its own.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词从一颗脑袋移到一个空间，因为空间被读作有自己的脾气。

senses.title: A spell of bad temper
senses.definition: a period of sulking or irritability, often named in the plural and with a possessive
senses.definitionCN: 一段闷气或易怒的时期，常以复数并带物主词出现
senses.example: He has been in one of his moods since the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 开会之后他一直闹着脾气。
senses.why: when the passing state is unpleasant, the plural turns it into a recurring event that others learn to expect.
senses.whyCN: 当这种会过去的状态并不愉快时，复数把它变成别人学会预期、一再发生的事。

senses.title: A grammatical category
senses.definition: the form of a verb that shows whether it states, commands or supposes
senses.definitionCN: 动词的形式，表明它是在陈述、命令还是假设
senses.example: English marks the imperative mood by leaving the subject out.
senses.exampleCN: 英语通过省去主语来标记祈使语气。
senses.why: this sense is a different word altogether, borrowed from Latin modus 'measure, manner', and it means a manner of speaking.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项其实是另一个词，借自拉丁 modus「尺度、方式」，意思是说话的方式。

senses.title: The public's temper
senses.definition: the general temper of a group, market or electorate at a given time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时刻一个群体、市场或选民的总体情绪
senses.example: The public mood turned against the plan within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 一周之内公众情绪就转向反对这个方案。
senses.why: one person's weather scaled up becomes a collective climate that politicians claim to read.
senses.whyCN: 一个人的天气放大之后成为集体的气候，政治家声称自己能读出它。

senses.title: Feeling like doing something
senses.definition: the inclination to do a particular thing at a particular moment
senses.definitionCN: 在某个时刻做某件具体事情的倾向
senses.example: She was not in the mood for another long explanation.
senses.exampleCN: 她没有兴致再听一段冗长的解释。
senses.why: the state is now aimed at an object, and 'in the mood for' turns a climate into a door that is either open or shut.
senses.whyCN: 这个状态现在有了对象，「有兴致」把气候变成一扇要么开、要么关的门。

senses.title: Rapid shifts of feeling
senses.definition: quick changes between emotional states, often treated as a symptom or a trait
senses.definitionCN: 情绪状态之间的快速变化，常被当作症状或特质
senses.example: Her mood swings made the household walk on glass.
senses.exampleCN: 她的情绪起落让全家人如履薄冰。
senses.why: the plural measures frequency, turning a state into a pattern that others can chart.
senses.whyCN: 复数衡量的是频率，把一个状态变成旁人能画出来的模式。

senses.title: The key of a work
senses.definition: the prevailing feeling that a painting, film or piece of music is built to produce
senses.definitionCN: 一幅画、一部电影或一段音乐被设计来产生的总体感受
senses.example: The grey palette gives the film a mood of waiting.
senses.exampleCN: 灰调子给这部片子一种等待的基调。
senses.why: artists speak of mood because a work also has weather, and the term lets them tune it deliberately.
senses.whyCN: 艺术家谈基调，是因为作品也有天气，而这个说法让他们能刻意调它。

intro.en: English has two different words written mood. The feeling word is native Old English mod 'mind, courage, temper'. The grammar word was borrowed later from Latin modus 'measure, manner', the same source as mode and model. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 英语里有两个写法相同的 mood。表感受的那个是本族古英语 mod「心、勇气、性情」；语法义的那个则是后来从拉丁 modus「尺度、方式」借入的，与 mode、model 同源。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mod meant 'mind, inner self, courage, anger'. It is Germanic in origin and had no connection with Latin at all.
items.cn: mod 意为「心、内在自我、勇气、愤怒」。它源出日耳曼语，与拉丁语毫无关联。

items.en: As the older senses faded, the word narrowed to a passing state of feeling, the sense it carries today.
items.cn: 随着较早的义项淡出，这个词收窄为一种会过去的感受状态，也就是今天的义项。

items.en: Modus meant 'measure, standard, manner'. Grammarians used it for the manner in which a verb states or commands, and that use entered English.
items.cn: modus 意为「尺度、标准、方式」。语法学家用它指动词陈述或命令的方式，这一用法进入了英语。

items.en: The spelling fell together in Middle English, so that one shape now carries two unrelated histories, one Germanic and one Latin.
items.cn: 两个词在中古英语里拼写合流，于是一个字形现在背着两段互不相关的历史，一段日耳曼，一段拉丁。

items.en: From the eighteenth century the feeling word was extended to rooms, crowds, markets and works of art, and mood music followed in the twentieth.
items.cn: 从 18 世纪起，表感受的那个词被延伸到屋子、人群、市场与艺术品，20 世纪又有了「氛围音乐」。

items.en: Source uncertain: the earliest written forms of the Germanic word are attested but its deeper pre-Germanic origin is a reconstruction, and no first date is agreed for the grammar borrowing.
items.cn: 来源不确定：那个日耳曼词的最早书写形式有书证，但它在日耳曼语之前的更深来源属重构形式；语法义借入的确切年代也没有公认结论。

note.en: Group one holds the word that looks the same but has another history; group two holds feeling words that differ in duration and cause.
note.cn: 第一组是字形相同而历史不同的词；第二组是持续时间与起因不同的感受词。

entries.definition: From Latin modus 'measure, manner': a way of doing something. It looks close to mood but shares history only with the grammar sense.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 modus「尺度、方式」：做事的方式。字形近 mood，但只与语法义共享历史。

entries.definition: Built on the feeling sense: given to sudden low or irritable states.
entries.definitionCN: 由表感受的义项构成：容易陷入突然的低落或烦躁。

entries.definition: Also from modus through a small form meaning 'little measure'; it belongs to design, not to feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 同样出自 modus，经由一个意为「小尺度」的形式；属设计领域，与感受无关。

entries.definition: From the same idea of measure: kept within limits. Nothing of it survives in the feeling word.
entries.definitionCN: 同出「尺度」这一观念：保持在限度之内。表感受的那个词里没有留下它的痕迹。

entries.definition: A distinct surge such as fear or joy; a mood is the longer weather that such surges happen inside.
entries.definitionCN: 如恐惧或喜悦那样一次明确的涌动；mood 是这些涌动所发生的更长的天气。

entries.definition: A settled tendency to become angry, closer to temperament than to a passing state.
entries.definitionCN: 易怒的固定倾向，更接近气质而非一时的状态。

entries.definition: The feel of a space or occasion; it covers the place sense but never the inner state of one person.
entries.definitionCN: 指空间或场合的感受；覆盖「地点」义，却从不指单个人的内在状态。

entries.definition: A plural word for how high or low someone's cheer is, as in high spirits; it measures level, not colour.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个人兴致高低的复数说法，如兴致高；衡量的是水位，而不是颜色。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The feeling sense is native Old English, while the grammar sense came from Latin modus, so one spelling hides two families.
normal.cn: 感受义是本族古英语，语法义则来自拉丁 modus，因此一个拼写藏着两个词族。

normal.en: The family runs mood, moody, moodily, moodiness, mood-altering, mood board.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mood、moody、moodily、moodiness、mood-altering、mood board。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: in a good mood, in the mood for, mood swings, set the mood.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：心情好、有兴致、情绪波动、定下气氛。

normal.en: Grammar keeps the Latin side alive in phrases like the imperative mood.
normal.cn: 语法在「祈使语气」一类说法里让拉丁那一面活着。

normal.en: Markets and newspapers speak of the public mood, extending one person's weather to a whole country.
normal.cn: 市场与报纸谈「公众情绪」，把一个人的天气扩到整个国家。

abstract.en: Picture a room where the lamp does not change but the walls seem to brighten and dim.
abstract.cn: 想象灯没有变，墙面却似乎忽明忽暗的屋子。

abstract.en: Picture a thermostat that responds to conversation rather than to air.
abstract.cn: 想象一个对谈话而不是对空气作出反应的恒温器。

abstract.en: Picture a door that opens only when the person inside feels like it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇只有在里面的人有兴致时才开的门。

examples.en: The mood in the office lifted as soon as the results arrived.
examples.cn: 结果一到，办公室里的气氛就轻松起来。

examples.en: I am not in the mood for a debate tonight.
examples.cn: 我今晚没兴致辩论。

examples.en: The subjunctive mood is rare in modern spoken English.
examples.cn: 虚拟语气在现代英语口语中很少见。

dict_mnemonic.text: mood 读如「木的」——人一时像木头一样闷着 → 心情、情绪、气氛

root: 两条独立来源：表感受的义项出自古英语 mod「心、勇气、性情」，属日耳曼语；表语气的语法义借自拉丁 modus「尺度、方式」，与 mode、model 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a person has weather, and that weather is then read as a room's temper, as a recurring bad spell, as a manner of speaking, as a public climate, as an open door, as a pattern of swings and finally as a key chosen by an artist.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个动作展开：人有天气，这天气依次被读作一间屋子的脾气、一再出现的坏脾气、一种说话方式、公众气候、一扇开着的门、一串起落的模式，最后是艺术家选定的调子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a room whose lamp never changes, yet the walls seem to brighten and dim as clouds cross the roof.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯始终没变的屋子，云从屋顶走过时墙面却忽明忽暗。

branches.en: WEATHER AND ITS RECORD: one sense is a single stretch of feeling, the other the chart of how often it turns.
branches.cn: 天气与它的记录：一个是单段感受，另一个是它翻转频率的图表。

branches.en: A SPACE WITH A TEMPER: the same weather either fills a room or is deliberately composed into a work.
branches.cn: 有脾气的空间：同一种天气要么充满一间屋子，要么被刻意编进一件作品。

branches.en: THE SPELL OTHERS LEARN: a bad mood made plural becomes a recurring event in a household.
branches.cn: 旁人学会的那阵子：坏心情一旦用复数，就成了一户人家反复发生的事。

branches.en: THE OTHER HISTORY: here the word does not mean feeling at all, but the manner in which a verb speaks.
branches.cn: 另一段历史：这里这个词完全不指感受，而指动词说话的方式。

branches.en: CLIMATE AND INCLINATION: one is a whole public's weather, the other a single door that is open or shut.
branches.cn: 气候与意愿：一个是整个公众的天气，另一个是单扇开或关的门。

intro.en: The word is short and native, so the interesting structure lies in its family and in the separate Latin homograph.
intro.cn: 这个词又短又是本族语，因此有意思的结构在它的词族，以及那个同形异源的拉丁词上。

latinIntro.en: Only the grammar sense has Latin behind it, from modus 'measure, manner'; the feeling word has no Latin ancestry at all.
latinIntro.cn: 只有语法义背后有拉丁语，出自 modus「尺度、方式」；表感受的那个词完全没有拉丁来历。

items.exampleCN: 它构成形容某人容易闹情绪的形容词。

items.meaning: given to low or irritable states
items.meaningCN: 容易陷入低落或烦躁的
items.exampleCN: 考试前他变得闷闷不乐。

items.example: It turns the adjective into a name for the trait.

items.meaning: the trait of changing mood quickly
items.exampleCN: 情绪多变在青春期很常见。

items.meaningCN: 为营造气氛而选的音乐
items.example: The café plays mood music all afternoon.
items.exampleCN: 这家咖啡馆整个下午放着氛围音乐。

items.example: The doctor asked about mood swings.
items.exampleCN: 医生询问了情绪波动的情况。

sceneCN: 这里 moon 指「绕地球运行的天然卫星，即月球」（第 1 个义项：地球的天然卫星）；句意为院墙上方，月亮已升到与屋瓦齐高。图中可辨识物件：院墙、圆月、屋脊、瓦片、淡蓝月色；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: The earth's natural satellite
senses.definition: the body that orbits the earth and causes tides and eclipses
senses.definitionCN: 绕地球运行、引起潮汐与食象的天体
senses.example: Above the courtyard wall, the moon has risen level with the roof tiles.
senses.exampleCN: 院墙上方，月亮已升到与屋瓦齐高。
senses.why: the word is native English, not borrowed, because the moon is the one sky object everyone could name without astronomy.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是英语本族词而非借词，因为月亮是无需天文学人人都会命名的天体。

senses.title: Its visible shape and phases
senses.definition: the moon as seen from earth, changing shape through the month
senses.definitionCN: 从地球所见的月亮，其形状在一个月里变化
senses.example: A thin crescent moon hung just above the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 一弯细细的月牙挂在山丘上方。
senses.why: what people call 'the moon' is usually the lit part they can see, so the word names an appearance as well as a body.
senses.whyCN: 人们所说的「月亮」通常指能看见的那部分亮面，因此这个词既指天体也指外观。

senses.title: Any planet's moon
senses.definition: a natural satellite of any planet, not only the earth's
senses.definitionCN: 任何行星的天然卫星，不限于地球的
senses.example: Jupiter's moons were the first found beyond our own.
senses.exampleCN: 木星的卫星是最早在我们月球之外被发现的。
senses.why: once Galileo saw four points circling Jupiter, the common noun extended from one moon to many.
senses.whyCN: 当伽利略看到四个光点绕木星后，这个普通名词便从一个月亮扩展到许多个。

senses.title: Moonlight
senses.definition: the light reflected from the moon, especially in literary use
senses.definitionCN: 月球反射的光，尤用于文学语言
senses.example: They walked home by the light of the moon.
senses.exampleCN: 他们借着月光走回家。
senses.why: since the moon's light is its most noticeable effect on earth, the noun easily stands for the light itself.
senses.whyCN: 月之光是对地球最显著的影响，因此这个名词很容易代指光本身。

senses.title: Many moons ago
senses.definition: in the fixed phrase many moons ago, meaning a long time in the past
senses.definitionCN: 固定短语「许多个月亮以前」，意为很久以前
senses.example: Many moons ago this field was an orchard.
senses.exampleCN: 很久以前，这片地是一座果园。
senses.why: a moon also meant a month, so counting moons was counting months, and the phrase keeps that older reckoning.
senses.whyCN: moon 也曾指一个月，因此数月亮就是数月份，这个短语保留了这种古老算法。

senses.title: To moon about
senses.definition: to spend time aimlessly or dreamily, as in mooning around the house
senses.definitionCN: 无所事事或恍恍惚惚地消磨时间，如在家里闲荡
senses.example: He mooned about the garden all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 他整个下午都在花园里闲荡。
senses.why: the verb pictures someone drifting like a moon across the sky, with no fixed direction.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词把人想成像月亮一样在天上漂移，没有固定方向。

senses.title: British slang: to moon
senses.definition: in informal British use, to show one's bare buttocks as a joke or insult
senses.definitionCN: 英式口语中，为玩笑或羞辱而露出光屁股
senses.example: The comedian mooned the crowd and was booed.
senses.exampleCN: 那个喜剧演员对观众露臀，被喝了倒彩。
senses.why: the slang sense plays on a pale round shape, but it is a separate development and should not be confused with the astronomy.
senses.whyCN: 这个俚语义借的是苍白圆形的样子，但它是独立发展出来的，不应与天文学义混淆。

senses.title: A lunar month
senses.definition: the period of the moon's cycle, about twenty-nine and a half days, once used to measure months
senses.definitionCN: 月亮盈亏一周的时长，约二十九天半，曾用来计量月份
senses.example: The festival follows the moon rather than the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节日按月亮而非太阳计算。
senses.why: month and moon come from the same root, so the calendar still carries the moon's cycle inside it.
senses.whyCN: month 与 moon 同出一根，因此历法里仍装着月亮的周期。

senses.title: Promise the moon
senses.definition: in idioms such as promise the moon, to offer something impossible
senses.definitionCN: 在「许诺月亮」等习语中，指许下不可能兑现的事
senses.example: Politicians promise the moon and deliver a lamp.
senses.exampleCN: 政客许诺月亮，却只送来一盏灯。
senses.why: the moon is visibly out of reach, which makes it the natural object for a promise no one can keep.
senses.whyCN: 月亮显然够不着，因此它自然成了无人能兑现的承诺的对象。

intro.en: Moon is native English, from Old English mōna, from Proto-Germanic *mēnô and a reconstructed Indo-European stem for 'moon, month'. It is not related to Latin luna. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: moon 是英语本族词，来自古英语 mōna、原始日耳曼语 *mēnô，再往前是表示「月亮、月份」的印欧词干重构形式。它与拉丁 luna 没有直接关系。年代均为约数。

items.en: Old English mōna named the moon and also stood for a month, a link still visible in month and Monday.
items.cn: 古英语 mōna 指月亮，也指一个月；这一联系仍见于 month 与 Monday。

items.en: The Proto-Germanic form *mēnô is reconstructed from the Germanic languages; no written record of it survives.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语形式 *mēnô 由各日耳曼语言重构而来，没有书面记录留存。

items.en: The stem usually written *mḗh₁n̥s meant both 'moon' and 'month' and is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: 通常写作 *mḗh₁n̥s 的词干兼指「月亮」与「月份」，属重构形式，并非有记录的词。

items.en: The same root idea connects the moon to measuring time, which is why month, Monday and 'many moons' all belong here.
items.cn: 同一词根把月亮与计时联系起来，因此 month、Monday 与「many moons」都属此处。

items.en: Latin luna 'moon' comes from a different root connected with light, and gives lunar, not moon.
items.cn: 拉丁 luna「月亮」来自另一个与光有关的词根，派生的是 lunar，而非 moon。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the exact Indo-European shape and its relation to the 'measure' root are debated, so the form given here is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：确切的印欧形态及其与「测量」词根的关系仍有争议，此处给出的形式属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same native stem; group two holds sky words that overlap in use.
note.cn: 第一组是同出本族词干的词；第二组是用法重叠的天空词。

entries.definition: A unit of the calendar, from the same root as moon; it names time, not the body.
entries.definitionCN: 历法单位，与 moon 同根；命名时间，而非天体。

entries.definition: Literally 'moon's day', a calque of Latin dies lunae; it keeps the older religious naming.
entries.definitionCN: 字面「月亮之日」，仿译拉丁 dies lunae；保留了更古老的宗教命名。

entries.definition: The light reflected by the moon; a compound, not a second object.
entries.definitionCN: 月球反射的光；是复合词，不指第二个天体。

entries.definition: A very small natural satellite; the -let suffix marks size, not kind.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的天然卫星；-let 后缀标记大小，而非种类。

entries.definition: The general word for any orbiting body, natural or artificial; moon is the everyday and native word.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何绕行天体，天然或人造；moon 是日常的本族词。

entries.definition: The curved shape of a waxing or waning moon; it names a phase, not the body.
entries.definitionCN: 盈缺月牙的弯曲形状；命名月相，而非天体。

entries.definition: The Latin-derived adjective for the moon; it replaces 'of the moon' in technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 源自拉丁的月球形容词；在技术文字中替代「月亮的」。

entries.definition: An old word for a heavenly light, especially sun or moon; it treats the moon as a lamp.
entries.definitionCN: 指天空发光体的旧词，尤指日月；把月亮当作一盏灯。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real relatives, real compounds and real idioms, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实同族词、真实搭配与真实习语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: moon and month share one root: a moon was a way of counting time.
normal.cn: moon 与 month 同根：月亮曾是计时方式。

normal.en: Monday is literally the moon's day.
normal.cn: Monday 字面就是「月亮之日」。

normal.en: The family runs moon, moons, moonlight, moonlit, moonlet, lunar.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 moon、moons、moonlight、moonlit、moonlet、lunar。

normal.en: Phases are fixed phrases: full moon, new moon, crescent moon, moon phase.
normal.cn: 月相是固定搭配：满月、新月、月牙、月相。

normal.en: Two idioms mark the word: many moons ago, once in a blue moon.
normal.cn: 两个习语标记这个词：很久以前、千载难逢。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp that changes its shape every night but never moves its post.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯每晚换形状，却从不挪动位置。

abstract.en: Picture a coin that is sometimes a thin edge and sometimes a full face.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币，有时只见薄边，有时见整面。

abstract.en: Picture a promise written on something nobody can reach.
abstract.cn: 想象把承诺写在一个谁也够不着的东西上。

examples.en: The moon rises about fifty minutes later each night.
examples.cn: 月亮每晚大约晚五十分钟升起。

examples.en: Saturn has more moons than any other planet.
examples.cn: 土星的卫星比任何其他行星都多。

examples.en: They met once in a blue moon, usually by the river.
examples.cn: 他们难得见一面，通常在河边。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「木嗯（moon）」——夜里抬头「嗯」一声看见的那轮圆盘 → 月亮

root: 古英语 mōna ← 原始日耳曼语 *mēnô ← 印欧词干 *mḗh₁n̥s（兼指月亮与月份，属重构形式）；与拉丁 luna 不同源，luna 另出与光有关的词根。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses keep one object but change the angle: the body, its visible phase, other planets' moons, its light, its use as a month, two verbs, a calendar cycle and an impossible promise.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项守着同一个天体，却不断换角度：天体、可见月相、别行星的卫星、它的光、它当月份、两个动词义、历法周期，以及一个够不着的承诺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round pale light above a wall, changing shape but staying in the sky.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙上方一轮淡色圆光，形状会变，却始终在天上。

branches.en: OBJECT AND LOOK: the same word names the body and the shape people see.
branches.cn: 天体与外观：同一个词既指天体，也指人们看见的形状。

branches.en: FROM ONE TO MANY: Galileo's four points made moon a countable class.
branches.cn: 从一到多：伽利略看到的四个光点使 moon 成为可数类别。

branches.en: LIGHT AND TIME: the moon gives light and once gave the month.
branches.cn: 光与时间：月亮给光，也曾给月份。

branches.en: IDIOMATIC REACH: counting moons measures the past, and promising one measures impossibility.
branches.cn: 习语中的尺度：数月亮量过去，许月亮量不可能。

branches.en: VERBAL DRIFT: drifting like a moon, and a slang joke on its pale round shape.
branches.cn: 动词漂移：像月亮一样漂，以及拿它苍白圆形开的俚语玩笑。

intro.en: Moon is a single native English root; its family is built by compounding and by the small suffix -let, not by Latin prefixes.
intro.cn: moon 是单一的英语本族词根；其词族靠复合与小型后缀 -let 构成，不用拉丁前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin used luna for the moon, a different root; English technical adjectives come from it, while the noun itself stays native.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 luna 指月亮，属另一词根；英语技术形容词由它而来，而名词本身仍是本族词。

items.example: The moon rose over the wall.

items.exampleCN: 探测器造访了数颗卫星。
他们穿过月光下的田野。

items.example: A moonlet orbits inside the ring.
items.exampleCN: 一颗小卫星在环内运行。

items.example: The moon landing was watched worldwide.
The month follows the moon's cycle.
Monday is named for the moon.

latinEntries.structure: dies lunae (noun phrase, fifth declension + genitive)
latinEntries.meaning: the day of the moon, Monday

definition_zh: 道德的；有道德的；寓意；道德准则
definition_en: concerned with right and wrong conduct, good in behaviour, and also the lesson drawn from a story or a set of principles
core_image: 心里那把量是非的尺子
scene: 篝火旁的寓言讲完，孩子们等着大人说出最后那句话。The fable ends with a simple moral about patience.
sceneCN: 这里是「寓意、教训」（第 3 个义项：故事传达的道理）；句意为这则寓言以一句关于耐心的浅显道理收尾。图中可辨识物件：篝火、故事书、围坐的孩子。

derivatives.zh: 由 moral 加 -ity 构成，义为「道德；道德体系」
由 moral 加 -ist 构成，义为「道德主义者；说教者」
由 moral 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「说教；从道德上解释」
由前缀 de-（去掉）加 moralize 构成，义为「使士气低落」

senses.title: Concerned with right and wrong
senses.definition: relating to principles of right and wrong behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 与行为对错的准则有关的
senses.example: Most people share a basic sense of moral duty.
senses.exampleCN: 多数人对道义责任有一种基本的感受。
senses.why: The Latin stem mor- named custom, and custom is exactly where a community's sense of right and wrong is stored.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词干 mor- 本指习俗，而一个群体对是非的判断正存放在习俗里。

senses.title: Good in behaviour
senses.definition: acting in a way that is considered good and honest
senses.definitionCN: 以被认为是善良诚实的方式行事
senses.example: He led a moral life and never cheated anyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他过着品行端正的生活，从不欺骗任何人。
senses.why: If custom supplies the standard, a person who follows it closely can be called moral, so the adjective moves from the rule to the person.
senses.whyCN: 既然习俗提供了标准，紧守标准的人就可以被称为有道德，于是形容词从规则转到了人身上。

senses.title: The lesson of a story
senses.definition: the point or lesson that a story or event is meant to teach
senses.definitionCN: 故事或事件想要教给人的要点或教训
senses.example: The moral of the story is that patience pays.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事的寓意是耐心会有回报。
senses.why: Fables were used to teach conduct, so the adjective's subject matter became a noun for the teaching itself.
senses.whyCN: 寓言本来是用来教人行为的，于是这个形容词所谈的内容就变成名词，指那番教导本身。

senses.title: Principles held by a person or group
senses.definition: the set of principles about right and wrong that someone or a group holds
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某群体所持的一套关于是非的原则
senses.example: She questioned the morals of the people around her.
senses.exampleCN: 她质疑身边那些人的道德准则。
senses.why: Customs can be counted one by one, so the plural names the separate rules a person carries.
senses.whyCN: 习俗可以一条一条地数，于是复数就指一个人所持有的那些具体准则。

intro.en: The word travels from a Latin noun for custom through Cicero's coinage and French into an English word for conduct and for the point of a story.
intro.cn: 这个词从拉丁语表示习俗的名词出发，经西塞罗的造词与法语，进入英语，用来指品行，也指故事的要点。

items.en: Latin mos, whose stem is mor-, meant custom or habitual manner, the unwritten rules a community lived by.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mos 的词干是 mor-，意为习俗或习惯做法，即一个群体赖以生活的成文之外的规矩。

items.en: Cicero is generally credited with coining moralis to render Greek ethikos, giving Latin a word for what concerns character and conduct.
items.cn: 一般认为 moralis 是西塞罗为翻译希腊语 ethikos 而造的，给拉丁语添了一个表示品行与行为的词。

items.en: Old French moral carried the adjective into everyday use for behaviour judged good or bad.
items.cn: 古法语 moral 把这个形容词带入日常使用，用来评判行为的好坏。

items.en: Middle English moral added the noun sense of a lesson drawn from a story, especially in fables.
items.cn: 中古英语的 moral 增加了名词义，指从故事、尤其是寓言中引出的教训。

items.en: Modern English moral works as an adjective for conduct and as a noun for the point of a tale or a set of principles.
items.cn: 现代英语的 moral 既是描述行为的形容词，也是指故事要点或一套原则的名词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same custom stem, while the near-meaning group collects adjectives of good conduct.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「习俗」词干上的词，近义组收描述良好品行的形容词。

entries.definition: The quality of being moral, or a system of moral rules.
entries.definitionCN: 由 moral 加 -ity 构成，义为「道德；道德体系」。

entries.definition: A person who teaches or studies moral rules.
entries.definitionCN: 讲授或研究道德准则的人。

entries.definition: The spirit and confidence of a group, from the same French stem but with a different sense.
entries.definitionCN: 一个群体的士气，同出法语词干但含义不同。

entries.definition: To take away someone's confidence or spirit.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人失去信心或士气。

entries.definition: Following accepted principles of right conduct.
entries.definitionCN: 遵循公认的正当行为原则的。

entries.definition: Showing high moral standards in behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 行为上体现高尚道德的。

entries.definition: Respectable and morally acceptable.
entries.definitionCN: 正派而合乎道德的。

entries.definition: Honest and morally correct in conduct.
entries.definitionCN: 为人诚实、行为端正的。

normalIntro.en: The family grows from a Latin noun for custom, and each branch keeps turning custom into a judgement about conduct.
normalIntro.cn: 这一族词从一个表示习俗的拉丁名词长出来，每个分支都把习俗变成对行为的评判。

normal.en: Latin mos, stem mor-, meant custom, so moral first described the customs a community shared.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mos 的词干是 mor-，意为习俗，所以 moral 最初描述一个群体共享的习俗。

normal.en: Cicero coined moralis for Greek ethikos, linking the word to character rather than to law.
normal.cn: 西塞罗为希腊语 ethikos 造出 moralis，把这个词与品行而非法律联系起来。

normal.en: morality adds -ity to moral: the quality of being concerned with right and wrong.
normal.cn: morality 在 moral 后加 -ity，指与是非有关的性质。

normal.en: The plural morals names the principles a person holds.
normal.cn: 复数的 morals 指一个人所持有的那些原则。

normal.en: The prefix de- in demoralize strips away the spirit that the stem once protected.
normal.cn: demoralize 里的前缀 de- 把词干曾经守护的那股气去掉。

abstract.en: A moral is a line drawn in the sand, and the point of a story is where the line sits.
abstract.cn: 道德是一条划在沙上的线，而故事的要点就是这条线画在哪里。

abstract.en: Customs harden into morals when a community stops asking why.
abstract.cn: 当一个群体不再追问为什么，习俗就凝固成道德。

abstract.en: The same stem gives morale, which shows how a shared mood and a shared code grow from one root.
abstract.cn: 同一词干还给出 morale，说明共同的士气与共同的准则如何从一条根上长出。

examples.en: Most people share a basic sense of moral duty.
examples.cn: 多数人对道义责任有一种基本的感受。

examples.en: The moral of the story is that patience pays.
examples.cn: 这个故事的寓意是耐心会有回报。

examples.en: She questioned the morals of the people around her.
examples.cn: 她质疑身边那些人的道德准则。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莫乱」——莫乱来，凡事讲道德；记住 moral 是道德的。

root: 拉丁语 mos（习俗、风气，词干 mor-）派生出 moralis，意为与品行有关的，经古法语 moral 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the standard drawn from custom; the senses then divide into good conduct itself, the lesson of a tale, and the countable rules a person holds.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是从习俗中画出的标准；义项由此分出端正的品行本身、故事的教训，以及一个人可数的那些准则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler held up against a person's conduct, marking what is allowed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把尺子举在一个人的行为前面，标出哪些是被允许的。

branches.en: a ruler laid across a decision
branches.cn: 一把尺子横在决定之上

branches.en: a person whose conduct never needs explaining
branches.cn: 一个行为从不需要解释的人

branches.en: the last line of a fable
branches.cn: 寓言结尾的那一句话

branches.en: a list of rules a family keeps
branches.cn: 一个家庭守着的一串规矩

branches.en: a tale that teaches a duty
branches.cn: 一则教人尽责的故事

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin noun for custom, a Latin adjective built from it, and two English endings that name its quality and its defenders.
intro.cn: 这个词依托一个表示习俗的拉丁名词、由它构成的拉丁形容词，以及两个分别指「性质」与「维护者」的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun mos and its derived moralis are the direct source of this whole English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 mos 及其派生的 moralis 是这一整族英语词的直接来源。

definition_zh: 道德上；从道德角度；有道德地；几乎确定地
definition_en: in terms of right and wrong, in a good and honest way, and in the fixed phrase morally certain, almost certainly
core_image: 把同一把尺子举到每个举动前面
scene: 会议室里有人把方案推回桌上，理由只有一句。She refused, on the grounds that the plan was morally wrong.
sceneCN: 这里是「道德上、从道德角度看」（第 1 个义项：按是非标准评判）；句意为她以这个计划在道德上站不住脚为由拒绝。图中可辨识物件：会议桌、方案纸、推回的手。

pos.zh: 道德上；从道德角度；有道德地

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词词尾 -ly 得到形容词 moral，义为「道德的」
由否定前缀 im- 加 moral 构成，义为「不道德的」
由 moral 加 -istic 构成，义为「说教的；道德主义的」

senses.title: Judged by a moral standard
senses.definition: in terms of right and wrong rather than of profit, taste or law
senses.definitionCN: 按是非来评判，而不是按利益、品味或法律
senses.example: The decision was morally defensible even if it was costly.
senses.exampleCN: 这个决定虽然在代价上不小，在道德上却站得住脚。
senses.why: -ly turns the adjective moral into a word for the standpoint from which something is judged.
senses.whyCN: -ly 把形容词 moral 变成表示「从哪个立足点评判」的词。

senses.title: In a good and honest way
senses.definition: in a way that follows accepted standards of good behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 以符合公认良好行为标准的方式
senses.example: They behaved morally when no one was watching.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人看着的时候，他们的行为依然正派。
senses.why: The same adverb can describe the manner of an act, not only the standard used, so it also means acting well.
senses.whyCN: 同一个副词既可以指所用的标准，也可以描述行为的方式，因此也能表示做得正派。

senses.title: Almost certain, in a fixed phrase
senses.definition: used in morally certain or morally sure to mean that something is almost certain to happen
senses.definitionCN: 用于 morally certain 或 morally sure，表示某事几乎肯定会发生
senses.example: It is morally certain that the vote will pass.
senses.exampleCN: 这次表决几乎肯定能通过。
senses.why: The phrase comes from legal and philosophical argument, where a conclusion could be certain for all practical purposes.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法来自法律与哲学的论辩，其中结论可以在一切实际意义上被视为确定。

intro.en: The adverb is a late, regular addition to moral, made with an Old English ending that had already been turning adjectives into adverbs for centuries.
intro.cn: 这个副词是后来在 moral 上按常规加缀构成的，所用的古英语词尾早已把形容词变成副词好几百年了。

items.en: The Latin adjective moralis described whatever concerned character and conduct, and it is the root of the whole family.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词 moralis 描述一切与品性和行为有关的东西，是这一整族词的根。

items.en: Old French passed the adjective moral to English, still judging behaviour as good or bad.
items.cn: 古法语把形容词 moral 传给英语，仍用来评判行为的好坏。

items.en: Middle English used moral for conduct and, as a noun, for the lesson of a story.
items.cn: 中古英语用 moral 指品行，也作名词指故事的教训。

items.en: The ending -ly descends from Old English -līce, which had long been the standard way to make an adverb from an adjective.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 源自古英语 -līce，早已是把形容词变成副词的标准方式。

items.en: Modern English morally adds that ending to moral and also carries the fixed phrase morally certain.
items.cn: 现代英语的 morally 把这一词尾加在 moral 上，并保留固定说法 morally certain。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms on the same moral stem, while the near-meaning group collects other adverbs of judgement.
note.cn: 形近组收同一道德词干上的形式，近义组收其他表示评判的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective from which this adverb is formed.
entries.definitionCN: 构成这个副词的原形容词。

entries.definition: In a way that goes against moral standards.
entries.definitionCN: 违背道德标准地。

entries.definition: Too concerned with judging other people's morals.
entries.definitionCN: 过分热衷于评判他人道德的。

entries.definition: In terms of accepted principles of conduct.
entries.definitionCN: 按公认的行为准则来看。

entries.definition: In a way that shows high moral standards.
entries.definitionCN: 以体现高尚道德的方式。

entries.definition: In a proper and respectable way.
entries.definitionCN: 以得体而正派的方式。

normalIntro.en: The word is an adverb of standard: it does not say what happened, only by which measure it should be weighed.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个关于标准的副词：它不说什么发生了，只说该用哪把尺子去称。

normal.en: morally is moral plus -ly, the adverb ending that descends from Old English -līce.
normal.cn: morally 是 moral 加 -ly，这个副词词尾源自古英语 -līce。

normal.en: The ending turns an adjective of judgement into a word for the manner of judging.
normal.cn: 这个词尾把表示评判的形容词变成表示评判方式的词。

normal.en: In morally wrong the adverb marks the standard being used, not the degree of wrongness.
normal.cn: 在 morally wrong 里，这个副词标出所用的是哪套标准，而不是错误的程度。

normal.en: The fixed phrase morally certain means almost certain, a sense that grew out of legal argument.
normal.cn: 固定说法 morally certain 意为几乎确定，这个含义从法律论辩中长出来。

normal.en: Immoral and morally share a stem: one judges the act, the other judges the manner.
normal.cn: immoral 与 morally 共用词干：一个评判行为，一个评判方式。

abstract.en: An adverb is a lens: morally tells you which lens is being held up.
abstract.cn: 副词像一片镜片：morally 告诉你举起的是哪一片。

abstract.en: The word asks not what happened but by which measure it is weighed.
abstract.cn: 这个词不问发生了什么，只问用哪把尺子去称。

abstract.en: A scale carried outside the body can become a habit carried inside.
abstract.cn: 身外的一杆秤，可以变成随身的一套习惯。

examples.en: The decision was morally defensible even if it was costly.
examples.cn: 这个决定虽然在代价上不小，在道德上却站得住脚。

examples.en: They behaved morally when no one was watching.
examples.cn: 没有人看着的时候，他们的行为依然正派。

examples.en: It is morally certain that the vote will pass.
examples.cn: 这次表决几乎肯定能通过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莫惹理」——莫惹道理，凡事从道德上讲；morally 是道德上。

root: 由 moral 加副词后缀 -ly 构成；-ly 源自古英语 -līce，长期用来把形容词变成副词。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is judging by a moral standard, and the two further senses cover acting well and the fixed use that means almost certain.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是按道德标准评判；另外两个义项分别覆盖做得正派，以及表示几乎确定的那种固定用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one ruler lifted in front of every act, always the same ruler.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一把尺子举在每一个举动前面，永远是同一把。

branches.en: a plan weighed against a rule
branches.cn: 一份方案被放到规则前称量

branches.en: a good deed done with no audience
branches.cn: 无人观看时做的一件好事

branches.en: a forecast that cannot realistically fail
branches.cn: 一个实际上不可能落空的预测

branches.en: a choice both defensible and clean
branches.cn: 一个既站得住脚又干净的选择

branches.en: a manner held to be beyond doubt
branches.cn: 被认为无可置疑的做法

intro.en: The word is a Latin adjective of conduct plus an Old English adverb ending, with a negative prefix close at hand.
intro.cn: 这个词是表示品行的拉丁形容词加古英语副词词尾，旁边还站着一个否定前缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin adjective moralis and its noun moralitas sit directly behind the English adjective and this adverb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形容词 moralis 及其名词 moralitas 直接位于英语形容词与这个副词的背后。

items.meaningCN: 把形容词变成副词的后缀

definition_zh: 而且；此外；再者（书面正式，表递进）
definition_en: used to add a further and usually stronger point to what has already been said, chiefly in formal writing
core_image: 评审表上第一条理由后面，又添上一条分量更重的新理由
scene: 评审意见先肯定方法可靠，随后又追加一条更有分量的理由。The method is reliable; moreover, it costs less than the old one.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（书面正式地递进补充第二点）；句意为这个方法可靠，而且比旧方法花费更少；对应第 1 个义项。

collocations.phrase: moreover, it should be noted that

derivatives.zh: 本词前半，由古英语表示「更多」的比较级演变而来，义为「更多；更」
本词后半，由古英语表示「在上、越过」的词演变而来，义为「在上方；越过」
与前半同词根的最高级形式，义为「最多；最」
由该最高级词干加副词词尾构成，义为「大多；主要地」

senses.title: Adding a further point
senses.definition: introducing an additional point that follows from or strengthens the previous one
senses.definitionCN: 引出另一点，它与前面的话相接或使前面的话更强
senses.example: The plan is cheap; moreover, it can be finished within one season.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案花费低，而且能在一个季节内完工。
senses.why: More adds quantity and over adds going beyond, so the adverb literally places another point on top.
senses.whyCN: 前半表「更多」，后半表「越过」，所以这个副词字面上就是把另一点摞在上面。

senses.title: Adding a stronger reason
senses.definition: used to bring in a reason that carries more weight than the one before
senses.definitionCN: 用来引入一个比前一条更有分量的理由
senses.example: The witness was credible; moreover, her account matched the records.
senses.exampleCN: 这名证人可信，而且她的陈述与记录相符。
senses.why: The word often marks not just addition but escalation, since the second point is meant to settle the matter.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常常不只表示添加，还表示加码，因为第二点意在把问题定下来。

senses.title: The second argument in a chain
senses.definition: introducing a parallel reason in a debate or a written argument
senses.definitionCN: 在论辩或书面论证中引入一条并列的理由
senses.example: The policy failed on cost; moreover, it failed on fairness.
senses.exampleCN: 这项政策在成本上失败，而且在公平性上也失败。
senses.why: Written argument stacks reasons in order, and the adverb signals that the stack is still growing.
senses.whyCN: 书面论证把理由按顺序摞起来，这个副词表示这一摞还在加高。

senses.title: Supporting evidence in academic prose
senses.titleCN: 学术文本中补充同向证据
senses.definition: used in research writing to add confirming evidence in the same direction
senses.definitionCN: 在研究写作中补上同方向的印证材料
senses.example: The samples were pure; moreover, repeated tests gave the same result.
senses.exampleCN: 样品是纯净的，而且反复测试给出了相同结果。
senses.why: Academic prose separates claims from support, and the word introduces a second piece of support.
senses.whyCN: 学术写作把论断与支撑分开，这个词引出第二份支撑材料。

senses.title: Cumulative conditions in rules
senses.definition: used in regulations and contracts to add another condition that must also hold
senses.definitionCN: 在规章与合同里再添一项也必须满足的条件
senses.example: The applicant must hold a licence; moreover, the licence must be current.
senses.exampleCN: 申请人必须持有许可证，而且该证必须仍在有效期内。
senses.why: Legal drafting accumulates requirements, and each added clause must be met as well as the earlier ones.
senses.whyCN: 法律起草会累积要求，每添一条都与前面诸条同样必须满足。

senses.title: Sentence-initial link across sentences
senses.definition: placed at the start of a new sentence to tie it to the previous one
senses.definitionCN: 放在新句子的开头，把该句与上一句绑在一起
senses.example: Moreover, the same rule applies to part-time staff.
senses.exampleCN: 此外，同一条规则也适用于兼职人员。
senses.why: A connective at the head of a sentence tells the reader how the new sentence relates to the old one.
senses.whyCN: 置于句首的连接词告诉读者新句子与旧句子是什么关系。

senses.title: Rhetorical escalation in speeches
senses.definition: used in public speech to raise the force of an argument step by step
senses.definitionCN: 在公开演讲中一步步抬高论点的力度
senses.example: The city needs more homes; moreover, it needs them now.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市需要更多住房，而且现在就需要。
senses.why: Spoken rhetoric uses the heavy adverb to make the second clause sound like the decisive one.
senses.whyCN: 口头论辩用这个厚重的副词，让第二个分句听起来像是决定性的那一个。

senses.title: Heavier register than its synonyms
senses.titleCN: 比同义说法更书面的语体
senses.definition: used where a formal tone is wanted, in contrast with lighter everyday connectives
senses.definitionCN: 用于需要正式语体的场合，与更轻的日常连接词形成对照
senses.example: Moreover is common in reports, whereas the shorter synonyms suit speech.
senses.exampleCN: 这个说法常见于报告，而较短的近义说法更适合口语。
senses.why: The word itself is a register signal: choosing it announces that the text is formal.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本身就是语体信号：选用它就宣告文本属于正式文体。

intro.en: Moreover is a native English compound of more, the comparative of much, and over, used as an intensifier. It is not a Latin borrowing, so the Latin entry list is empty.
intro.cn: 这是英语本土复合词，由表示「多」的比较级与作加强成分的「在上、越过」合成，并非拉丁语借词，因此拉丁词条列表为空。

items.en: Māra was the comparative of the word for much, and it supplies the first element.
items.cn: 古英语中表示「多」的比较级提供了第一个成分。

items.en: Ofer meant over or beyond, and in compounds it adds the sense of going further.
items.cn: 这个词意为在上、越过，在复合词中增添「更进一步」的意思。

items.en: The two words first appeared as a phrase meaning beyond that, further, before they merged.
items.cn: 两词先以短语形式出现，义为「在那之外、更进一步」，后来才合并。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the merged adverb stood at the head of a sentence to add a point; its exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个合并的副词已站在句首用来追加论点；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Today it belongs to formal prose and public argument and sounds heavier than its shorter rivals.
items.cn: 今天它属于正式文章与公共论辩，听起来比更短的近义说法更重。

note.en: The first group shares the compound structure or the same root; the second group lists connectives that also add a point.
note.cn: 第一组共享复合结构或同一词根；第二组是同样用于追加论点的连接词。

entries.definition: A formal connective with the same job, built from further and more.
entries.definitionCN: 一个作用相同的正式连接词，由「更远」与「更多」构成。

entries.definition: The comparative that supplies the first half of the word.
entries.definitionCN: 提供这个词前半部分的比较级形式。

entries.definition: The second half, adding the sense of beyond or on top.
entries.definitionCN: 后半部分，增添「越过、在上」的意思。

entries.definition: The superlative of the same root, meaning the greatest amount.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根的最高级，义为最多。

entries.definition: An adverb from the same root, meaning for the greater part.
entries.definitionCN: 同词根的副词，义为大部分情况下。

entries.definition: A lighter connective that adds a point, often in speech and often with a hint of afterthought.
entries.definitionCN: 语气更轻的追加连接词，多用于口语，常带「顺带一提」的意味。

entries.definition: A plain phrase that adds an item without raising the tone.
entries.definitionCN: 朴素的追加短语，只添一项，不抬高语气。

entries.definition: An emphatic phrase that adds a stronger consideration.
entries.definitionCN: 强调式短语，用来追加更有分量的考虑。

entries.definition: A conversational phrase for one more point stacked on the rest.
entries.definitionCN: 口语短语，表示在其余之上再加一点。

entries.definition: An adverb that pushes the argument one step farther.
entries.definitionCN: 把论证再往前推一步的副词。

normalIntro.en: More plus over: one point is placed over and beyond the first, and the compound says exactly that.
normalIntro.cn: 「更多」加「越过」：把一点摞到第一点之上并越过它，这个复合词说的正是这件事。

normal.en: Stack two bricks: the second sits higher and presses the first down.
normal.cn: 两块砖叠起来：第二块位置更高，并把第一块压住。

normal.en: It always takes a comma right after it when it opens a sentence.
normal.cn: 它放在句首时，后面总要跟一个逗号。

normal.en: In reports it replaces the spoken phrase for and also.
normal.cn: 在报告里，它替代口语中表示「而且还有」的说法。

normal.en: It never inflects; only its position in the sentence changes.
normal.cn: 它从不发生词形变化，变的只是它在句子里的位置。

normal.en: A reviewer writes it when the first reason was not quite enough.
normal.cn: 评审人写它，往往是因为第一条理由还不够。

abstract.en: A second reason is not a repetition; it is new weight on the same scale.
abstract.cn: 第二条理由不是重复，而是同一杆秤上新加的砝码。

abstract.en: Formal writing uses a signpost that admits it is adding something.
abstract.cn: 正式写作会用一块指路牌，坦白说明自己正在添加内容。

abstract.en: To say moreover is to promise that the next sentence earns its place.
abstract.cn: 说出这个词，就等于承诺下一句配得上它的位置。

examples.en: The plan is cheap; moreover, it can be finished within one season.
examples.cn: 这个方案花费低，而且能在一个季节内完工。

examples.en: Moreover, the same rule applies to part-time staff.
examples.cn: 此外，同一条规则也适用于兼职人员。

examples.en: The samples were pure; moreover, repeated tests gave the same result.
examples.cn: 样品是纯净的，而且反复测试给出了相同结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「莫罗佛」——「莫」是更多，「罗佛」是越过去，多上加多、层层加码：而且、此外

root: 英语本土复合词，由古英语表示「更多」的比较级与表示「在上、越过」的词合成，十六世纪起用作句首副词；确切书面首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from a simple added point through a stronger reason, a parallel argument, academic evidence, cumulative rules, sentence linking, rhetorical escalation and the word's own formal tone.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从单纯追加一点，依次走向更强的理由、并列论据、学术证据、累积条款、跨句衔接、修辞加码，最后落到这个词本身的正式语体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a review sheet where a second, heavier reason is written under the first.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张评审表，第一条理由下面又写上了分量更重的第二条。

branches.en: THE ADDED POINT: a further statement is attached, often at the head of the next sentence.
branches.cn: 追加的一点：再添一句，常置于下一句句首。

branches.en: THE STRONGER PUSH: the new point carries more weight and raises the tone.
branches.cn: 更强的一推：新论点分量更重，也抬高语气。

branches.en: THE SECOND ARGUMENT: a parallel reason stands beside the first in a debate.
branches.cn: 第二条论据：论辩中与第一条并立的理由。

branches.en: THE EXTRA EVIDENCE: academic prose adds confirming data in the same direction.
branches.cn: 额外证据：学术文字补上同方向的印证数据。

branches.en: THE CUMULATIVE RULE AND THE HEAVY TONE: conditions stack in documents, and the word itself marks formal register.
branches.cn: 累积条款与厚重语体：文书里条件层层叠加，这个词本身就标记正式语体。

intro.en: Moreover is a native compound, so its parts are ordinary English words rather than affixes. The items below show the compound and its family.
intro.cn: 这是本族复合词，组成部分是普通英语词而非词缀。下列条目展示这一复合词及其词族。

latinIntro.en: There are no Latin entries: the word is built from Old English elements and has no Latin or Greek ancestor. The list is left empty on purpose.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁词条：这个词由古英语成分构成，没有拉丁或希腊语祖先，清单按设计留空。

items.example: The compound itself adds a point.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词本身表示追加一点。

items.example: A parallel compound with the same function.
items.exampleCN: 一个功能相同的并列复合词。

items.example: It adds a point in a lighter tone.
items.exampleCN: 它以更轻的语气追加一点。

items.example: It shares the root of the first element.
The adverb ending turns the superlative into a modifier.
items.exampleCN: 副词词尾把最高级变成修饰语。

items.meaning: at the head of a clause, with a comma
items.example: Position alone signals that a new point is coming.
items.exampleCN: 仅靠位置就能提示有新论点要来。

derivatives.zh: 本词前半，义为「更多」
同一词根的最高级，义为「最多」
由最高级词干加副词词尾构成，义为「大多」
本词后半，义为「在上；越过」

definition_zh: 早晨；上午；黎明；开端
definition_en: the early part of the day from sunrise to noon, also dawn itself and the opening phase of something
core_image: 窗帘缝里透进来的第一道光
scene: 天还没亮，海面上只剩雾和远处一盏航标灯。By morning the fog had lifted off the harbour.
sceneCN: 这里是「早晨、上午」（第 1 个义项：天亮到中午前的一段时间）；句意为到天亮时雾已从港口散去。图中可辨识物件：海雾、航标灯、码头。

derivatives.zh: 去掉词尾 -ing 得到的书面短形式，义为「晨」
同一词干保留较早含义，义为「次日」
由 morning 与 glory 复合，指清晨开放的牵牛花

senses.title: The early part of the day
senses.definition: the time from sunrise until noon
senses.definitionCN: 从日出到中午的一段时间
senses.example: The market opens early in the morning.
senses.exampleCN: 市场在清晨就开门了。
senses.why: The Germanic word named the hours when light returns, and English kept that plain, everyday sense as the core.
senses.whyCN: 这个日耳曼词本来指光回来的那段时间，英语把这个朴素的日常含义保留为核心。

senses.title: Dawn itself
senses.definition: the moment when the sky first grows light
senses.definitionCN: 天空开始变亮的那一刻
senses.example: Morning came slowly over the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 曙色慢慢越过群山。
senses.why: Because the word first meant the turning of the night, it can name the single moment of first light rather than the whole morning.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指夜色转折的那一刻，所以它能指第一道光的瞬间，而不只是整个上午。

senses.title: The opening phase of something
senses.definition: the early stage of a period, thought of as its dawn
senses.definitionCN: 一个时期的早期阶段，被看作它的黎明
senses.example: The morning of the industry was full of wild experiments.
senses.exampleCN: 这个行业的初期充满了大胆的试验。
senses.why: If a day begins with a morning, any period can be given a morning, so the word becomes a metaphor for beginnings.
senses.whyCN: 一天以早晨开场，任何时期也就可以有一个早晨，于是这个词成了开端的比喻。

senses.title: A morning greeting
senses.definition: used in the greeting good morning
senses.definitionCN: 用于问候语 good morning 之中
senses.example: He called out a cheerful good morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他高声说了一句爽朗的早上好。
senses.why: A greeting names the time it belongs to, so morning became part of a fixed social formula.
senses.whyCN: 问候语会用它所属的时间来命名，于是早晨就成了一个固定社交用语的一部分。

intro.en: The word began as a Germanic name for the light-returning hours and gained its ending in Middle English by analogy with the word for evening.
intro.cn: 这个词最初是日耳曼语中对光线回归时段的称呼，在中古英语里仿照表示傍晚的词补上了词尾。

items.en: A reconstructed form generally taken as murganaz is the common Germanic ancestor of the words for morning.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个重构形式 murganaz 是日耳曼各语言中表示早晨的词的共同祖先。

items.en: Old English morgen meant morning and could also point to the next day, a sense that survives in morrow.
items.cn: 古英语 morgen 意为早晨，也能指次日，这个含义仍留在 morrow 里。

items.en: Middle English added the ending -ing to morwen, producing morweninge, perhaps by analogy with evening.
items.cn: 中古英语在 morwen 后加上词尾 -ing，形成 morweninge，这也许是仿照 evening 的结果。

items.en: By the early modern period the form had shortened to morning and the greeting good morning was fixed.
items.cn: 到近代早期，这个词形已缩短为 morning，问候语 good morning 也固定下来。

items.en: Modern English morning names the early hours and, figuratively, the opening phase of anything.
items.cn: 现代英语的 morning 指清早的几个小时，也比喻任何事物的开端阶段。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms on the same old stem or built with the same ending, while the near-meaning group collects the words for first light.
note.cn: 形近组收同一古老词干上的形式或用了相同词尾的形式，近义组收表示初光的词。

entries.definition: A literary shortening of morning.
entries.definitionCN: morning 的书面缩短形式。

entries.definition: The next day, from the older sense of the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 次日，来自同一词干的较早含义。

entries.definition: The matching time word for the end of the day, built with a similar ending but a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 与早晨相对的一天尾声用词，结尾形式相似但词根不同。

entries.definition: The first light of day.
entries.definitionCN: 一天中的第一道光。

entries.definition: The part of the day before noon, a formal word.
entries.definitionCN: 中午之前的那段时间，较书面。

entries.definition: The moment when daylight begins.
entries.definitionCN: 天亮的那一刻。

normalIntro.en: The word grew from a Germanic name for the returning light, and its family keeps the sense of a day turning over.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从日耳曼语中表示光线回归的名称长出来，同族词都保留着一天翻页的感觉。

normal.en: Old English morgen is the base, and Middle English added -ing, much as evening was formed.
normal.cn: 古英语 morgen 是底子，中古英语加上 -ing，很像 evening 的构成方式。

normal.en: morrow, meaning the next day, keeps the older sense of morgen as tomorrow.
normal.cn: morrow 意为次日，保留了 morgen 指明天的较早含义。

normal.en: Good morning is a fixed greeting, so the word also names a social ritual.
normal.cn: good morning 是固定问候语，所以这个词也指一种社交礼节。

normal.en: The plural mornings appears in phrases like early mornings, naming repeated occasions.
normal.cn: 复数的 mornings 出现在 early mornings 一类短语里，指反复出现的清晨。

normal.en: morning-glory is a compound: a flower that opens with the day.
normal.cn: morning-glory 是复合词，指随白天开放的花。

abstract.en: Morning is the word for light returning to the same room.
abstract.cn: 早晨就是光回到同一间屋子的那个词。

abstract.en: Every morning is a page with nothing written on it yet.
abstract.cn: 每个早晨都是一张还没写上字的纸。

abstract.en: The word carries both a clock and a beginning, which is why a career can have a morning.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时装着钟点和开端，所以一段事业也可以有它的早晨。

examples.en: The market opens early in the morning.
examples.cn: 市场在清晨就开门了。

examples.en: Morning came slowly over the hills.
examples.cn: 曙色慢慢越过群山。

examples.en: He called out a cheerful good morning.
examples.cn: 他高声说了一句爽朗的早上好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摸宁」——摸黑等到天亮，四周变宁；记住 morning 是早晨。

root: 中古英语 morweninge 由 morwen（早晨，源自古英语 morgen）加 -ing 构成，一般认为模仿了 evening 的形式。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the early hours; the senses then divide into first light, the opening phase of anything, and the fixed greeting.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是清早的时段；义项由此分出第一道光、万事万物的开端阶段，以及固定问候语中的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first beam slipping through a gap in the curtains onto the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：第一道光从窗帘缝隙里滑进来，落在地板上。

branches.en: a kitchen lit before the street wakes
branches.cn: 街上还没醒，厨房先亮了

branches.en: first light touching the water
branches.cn: 初光落在水面上

branches.en: the first years of a movement
branches.cn: 一场运动的头几年

branches.en: a greeting exchanged at the gate
branches.cn: 在门口交换的一句问候

branches.en: fog lifting as the day turns
branches.cn: 天翻页时散去的雾

intro.en: The word joins an old Germanic noun for morning with a noun ending shared by other time words, and it still splits into short and compound forms.
intro.cn: 这个词把日耳曼语中表示早晨的古名词与一个和其他时间词共用的名词词尾接在一起，并且还分出缩短形式与复合形式。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word, so the Latin side is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，因此拉丁语部分留空。

a flower that opens at dawn

definition_zh: 抵押贷款；抵押
definition_en: a loan secured against a property; to give property as security for a debt
core_image: 一所房子，它的地基被一根粗粗的锁链拴在银行大楼上
scene: 年轻人刚领到第一张工资单，银行顾问就在桌上摊开了一份写满数字的长合同。They took out a mortgage to buy their first apartment.
sceneCN: 这里 mortgage 指「抵押贷款」（第 1 个义项：以房产为担保的借款）；句意为他们通过按揭贷款买了第一套公寓。图中可辨识物件：房屋平面图、银行合同、工资单；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 抵押人
抵押权人
抵押支持的
出借抵押贷款的人/机构

senses.title: loan secured on property
senses.definition: a long-term loan for which the borrower's property serves as security
senses.definitionCN: 以借款人的房产作为担保的长期贷款
senses.example: Most people need a mortgage to buy a home.
senses.exampleCN: 多数人买房需要按揭。
senses.why: The house pledges its value until the debt dies, matching the etymology.
senses.whyCN: 房子把自己的价值押上去，直到债务消失，正好对应词源。

senses.title: the act of securing
senses.definition: the legal act of giving property as security for a debt
senses.definitionCN: 以财产为债务作担保的法律行为
senses.example: The mortgage was recorded at the county registry.
senses.exampleCN: 抵押登记被记入县登记处。
senses.why: The noun of the act follows from the loan it creates.
senses.whyCN: 行为的名词义从它所产生的贷款衍生而来。

senses.title: to pledge property
senses.definition: to give property as security for a loan
senses.definitionCN: 把财产押出去作贷款的担保
senses.example: They mortgaged their cottage to fund the business.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把小木屋抵押出去以资助生意。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb by a usual shift.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成动词，是常见的词类转换。

senses.title: a particular loan product
senses.definition: a specific mortgage arrangement such as fixed-rate, variable, or balloon
senses.definitionCN: 固定利率、浮动、气球贷等具体安排
senses.example: An adjustable-rate mortgage suited their short stay.
senses.exampleCN: 可调整利率的 mortgage 适合他们短期居住的需求。
senses.why: The general term names one design of the same contract.
senses.whyCN: 通用术语被用来指同一种合同的某种设计。

senses.title: debt burden, figuratively
senses.definition: a heavy or long-lasting financial burden
senses.definitionCN: 沉重或长期的财务负担
senses.example: His student loan feels like a mortgage on his future.
senses.exampleCN: 他的助学贷款就像给未来押了一份按揭。
senses.why: A lasting debt mirrors the long-term house loan.
senses.whyCN: 一笔长期债务和长期房贷在形状上相似。

senses.title: commercial property loan
senses.definition: a loan secured against a non-residential building or land
senses.definitionCN: 以非住宅建筑或土地为担保的贷款
senses.example: The developer used a commercial mortgage for the tower.
senses.exampleCN: 开发商用商业抵押贷款建起了那座塔楼。
senses.why: The same legal tool serves business property too.
senses.whyCN: 同一种法律工具也适用于商业物业。

senses.title: the security instrument
senses.definition: the legal document that sets out the pledge of property
senses.definitionCN: 规定财产抵押的法律文件
senses.example: The mortgage had to be signed by both spouses.
senses.exampleCN: 抵押契据必须由夫妻双方签字。
senses.why: The act creates the paper that records it.
senses.whyCN: 行为产生了记录它的那张纸。

senses.title: death pledge, literal etymology
senses.definition: a pledge that dies when the debt is repaid
senses.definitionCN: 当债务还清时即终止的质押
senses.example: The etymology points to mortgage = mort (dead) + gage (pledge).
senses.exampleCN: 词源指出 mortgage = mort（死）+ gage（誓约）。
senses.why: The etymology re-surfaces as a learnt sense.
senses.whyCN: 词源学把它重新作为一个学术义项提出来。

intro.en: Mortgage literally means 'death pledge'. It comes from Old French mort 'dead' and gage 'pledge', because the pledge dies when the debt is repaid.
intro.cn: Mortgage 字面上就是「死誓」。来自古法语 mort「死」与 gage「誓约、抵押」，因为债务还清后这份质押就「死了」。

items.en: Old French mort meant 'dead'; it comes from Latin mors 'death'.
items.cn: 古法语 mort 意为「死的」，来自拉丁语 mors「死亡」。

items.en: Old French gage meant 'pledge, warranty'; it came from Frankish *wagjo 'pledge'.
items.cn: 古法语 gage 意为「誓约、担保」，来自法兰克语 *wagjo「抵押」。

items.en: Old French mortgage was used in law by the 12th century for a pledge that ends (dies) when the debt is settled.
items.cn: 古法语 mortgage 在 12 世纪已用于法律，指债务清偿后即终止的质押。

items.en: The word entered English through the Normans in the 14th century, spelled morgage at first.
items.cn: 诺曼人把这个词带入英语，14 世纪刚进入时拼作 morgage。

items.en: By the 20th century it became the standard term for home loan; subprime mortgage appeared in the 1990s.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪它成为房贷的标准说法；subprime mortgage 次级按揭在 1990 年代出现。

items.en: Solid etymology: mort and gage are both well attested. The Frankish *wagjo is a reconstructed root but widely accepted.
items.cn: 词源可靠：mort 与 gage 均有充分佐证。法兰克语 *wagjo 为构拟形式但被广泛接受。

note.en: Look-alikes share the -gage ending; near meanings are neighbouring ways to borrow against property.
note.cn: 形近是共用 -gage 结尾的词；近义是邻近的以财产借贷的方式。

entries.definition: From French gantelet 'little glove'; not from mortgage at all.
entries.definitionCN: 来自法语 gantelet「小手套」；与 mortgage 无关。

entries.definition: A regular payment for work; shares the *wagjo root of gage 'pledge'.
entries.definitionCN: 工资；与 gage 同出法兰克语 *wagjo。

entries.definition: To measure or a measurement; possibly related to gage 'pledge' through notion of 'guaranteed measurement'.
entries.definitionCN: 测量或量具；可能通过「确定的度量」与 gage 相连。

entries.definition: To humiliate; from Latin mors 'death' + facere 'make'.
entries.definitionCN: 羞辱；来自 mors「死」+ facere「制造」。

entries.definition: Property pledged for a loan; mortgage is the loan itself secured by it.
entries.definitionCN: 贷款质押的财产；mortgage 是以它作担保的贷款。

entries.definition: Any borrowing; mortgage is a specific long-term property-secured loan.
entries.definitionCN: 任何借款；mortgage 是特定的长期房产担保借款。

entries.definition: A US alternative to mortgage where a trustee holds the property.
entries.definitionCN: 美国替代 mortgage 的形式，由受托人持有物业。

entries.definition: A loan against the equity in your house, a kind of second mortgage.
entries.definitionCN: 以房屋净值为抵押的贷款，是 second mortgage 的一种。

normalIntro.en: Real morphemes and fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与固定搭配。

normal.cn: mort（死）+ gage（誓约）= 死誓；债没了，誓也没了。

normal.cn: mort 与 mortal、mortify、immortal 同根。

normal.cn: gage 与 wage（以工作换抵押）同根。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: take out a mortgage, pay off a mortgage.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：take out a mortgage 申请按揭、pay off 还清。

normal.en: Subprime mortgage became infamous in 2008.
normal.cn: 2008 年 subprime mortgage 臭名远扬。

abstract.en: Picture a house with a little tombstone in front of it that disappears when the debt is paid.
abstract.cn: 想象一座房子前面有块小墓碑，还清债务时墓碑就消失了。

abstract.en: Picture a couple signing their lives away at a mortgage broker's desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一对情侣在按揭经纪人的桌上签下自己的人生。

abstract.en: Picture a Latin-speaking banker saying 'this pledge will die with the debt'.
abstract.cn: 想象一个会说拉丁语的银行家说「这份誓约会随债一同死掉」。

examples.en: A jump in mortgage rates sent the housing market into a slump.
examples.cn: 按揭利率一跳高，房地产市场就陷入低迷。

examples.en: They mortgaged the family farm to pay for their daughter's cancer treatment.
examples.cn: 他们把家族农场抵押出去，为女儿的癌症治疗筹钱。

examples.en: Many homeowners found themselves underwater when their mortgage exceeded the house value.
examples.cn: 许多房主发现自己的负债超过了房屋价值。

sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从贷款本身 → 行为 → 动词 → 某一类型 → 比喻的负担 → 商业物业 → 合同文书 → 词源学上的「死誓」。

definition_zh: 蚊子；蚊虫滋扰；蚊媒疾病的传播者；蚊的幼虫（作定语）；蚊帐等防蚊用品（作定语）；小型舰艇编队（蚊队）；蚊叮的小伤；被当作猎物的小飞虫（如蚊鹰）
definition_en: a small two-winged fly whose female bites and sucks blood, often carrying disease; also used of the nuisance, the diseases it spreads and small craft fleets
core_image: 水面上倒立着一只细腿小虫，口器像一根细针，背后是静止的池水与一圈涟漪
scene: 池塘边，一只蚊子把细长的口器刺进人的前臂。A mosquito pierces the skin of a sleeper's forearm with its needle-like mouthparts.
sceneCN: 这里 mosquito 指「吸血的小型双翅目昆虫」（第 1 个义项：蚊）；句意为一只蚊子用针状口器刺入睡者前臂的皮肤。可辨识物件：细长口器、透明翅膀、前臂、池水；对应第 1 个义项。
