senses.title: A small blood-sucking fly
senses.titleCN: 蚊子：吸血的小型双翅目昆虫
senses.definition: a small two-winged fly whose female pierces skin and takes blood
senses.definitionCN: 雌虫刺穿皮肤吸血的细小双翅目昆虫
senses.example: A mosquito pierces the skin of a sleeper's forearm with its needle-like mouthparts.
senses.exampleCN: 一只蚊子用针状口器刺入睡者前臂的皮肤。
senses.why: Only the female bites, because she needs blood protein for her eggs; the everyday word still names the whole insect.
senses.whyCN: 只有雌虫叮咬，因为它需要血液中的蛋白质来产卵；日常用词仍指整个虫体。

senses.title: A biting nuisance
senses.definition: mosquitoes treated collectively as an irritating swarm that drives people indoors
senses.definitionCN: 把蚊虫看成一群扰人的飞虫，能把人赶进屋里
senses.example: The mosquitoes drove the whole camp indoors before dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 蚊群还没到黄昏就把整个营地的人赶进了屋。
senses.why: When the plural is used this way, the word names an annoyance rather than a species.
senses.whyCN: 复数这样用时，词指的是扰人的麻烦，而不是某个物种。

senses.title: A disease vector
senses.definition: the insect understood as the carrier that passes malaria, dengue or other infections between people
senses.definitionCN: 被理解为在人与人之间传递疟疾、登革热等感染的媒介昆虫
senses.example: Mosquitoes carry malaria in lowland regions.
senses.exampleCN: 蚊子在低地地区传播疟疾。
senses.why: Public health shifted the emphasis from the bite to the transmission chain, and this sense now dominates medical writing.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生把重点从叮咬转到传播链，这一义如今在医学写作中占主导。

senses.title: The aquatic young stage
senses.definition: the larval form that hangs at the water surface, usually named in the compound mosquito larva
senses.definitionCN: 倒悬在水面的幼虫，通常以「mosquito larva」这一复合形式出现
senses.example: Mosquito larvae hang head-down just beneath the surface film.
senses.exampleCN: 孑孓头朝下挂在表面水膜之下。
senses.why: The adult name is reused as a modifier for its own young, a common pattern in entomology.
senses.whyCN: 成虫名被复用作自身幼期的修饰语，这是昆虫学中常见的模式。

senses.title: Protective gear against mosquitoes
senses.definition: the equipment named after the insect, such as a mosquito net, coil or repellent
senses.definitionCN: 以这种昆虫命名的防护用品，如蚊帐、蚊香或驱蚊剂
senses.example: A mosquito net over the bed is the cheapest protection.
senses.exampleCN: 床上挂一顶蚊帐是最便宜的防护。
senses.why: The word marks what the object is used against, so the insect name becomes a label for the defence.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标出物件用来对付什么，昆虫名于是成了防护手段的标签。

senses.title: A fleet of small craft
senses.definition: a group of tiny, fast boats or warships, historically called a mosquito fleet
senses.definitionCN: 一群小而快的船或军舰，历史上称作蚊队
senses.example: A mosquito fleet of wooden gunboats patrolled the river.
senses.exampleCN: 一支由木制炮艇组成的蚊队巡弋河面。
senses.why: The metaphor compares small, numerous, stinging craft to a swarm of biting insects.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把数量多、体量小、能刺痛人的舰艇比作一群叮人的虫。

senses.title: A small irritating wound
senses.definition: the itchy swelling left by a bite, commonly called a mosquito bite
senses.definitionCN: 叮咬留下的发痒肿块，通常说成「mosquito bite」
senses.example: A mosquito bite on his ankle kept him awake.
senses.exampleCN: 脚踝上的蚊叮让他一夜没睡好。
senses.why: Metonymy moves the name from the biter to the mark it leaves, a very common shift in medical everyday speech.
senses.whyCN: 转喻把名字从叮咬者移到留下的痕迹，这是医学口语中极常见的转移。

senses.title: A tiny flying prey
senses.titleCN: 被当作猎物的小飞虫（如蚊鹰）
senses.definition: a small flying insect understood as food for a predator, as in the folk name mosquito hawk
senses.definitionCN: 被看作捕食者食物的小飞虫，如俗称蚊鹰的蜻蜓
senses.example: Children call the dragonfly a mosquito hawk because it catches small flies.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们把蜻蜓叫作蚊鹰，因为它捕食小飞虫。
senses.why: Here mosquito names the prey, and the compound tells what the larger insect feeds on.
senses.whyCN: 此处 mosquito 指猎物，复合词说明那种更大的昆虫吃什么。

intro.en: Mosquito is a Spanish and Portuguese diminutive of mosca 'fly', from Latin musca. English borrowed it in the sixteenth century during exploration of the Americas.
intro.cn: mosquito 是西班牙语与葡萄牙语中 mosca「苍蝇」的指小形式，源自拉丁 musca。英语在 16 世纪探索美洲期间把它借入。

items.en: Latin musca meant 'fly'; its own deeper origin is not settled, and the Indo-European forms sometimes cited for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: 拉丁 musca 意为「苍蝇」；它更深的来源并无定论，偶尔为其引用的印欧形式属重构。

items.en: Spanish and Portuguese added the diminutive suffix -ito to mosca, giving mosquito 'little fly', the form English borrowed.
items.cn: 西班牙语与葡萄牙语给 mosca 加上指小后缀 -ito，构成 mosquito「小苍蝇」，英语借的就是这一形式。

items.en: English recorded mosquito in the late sixteenth century in travel accounts of the Caribbean and South America.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪后期的加勒比与南美游记中记录了 mosquito。

items.en: After the discovery that the insect transmits malaria and yellow fever, the word moved into public health vocabulary in the late nineteenth century.
items.cn: 在发现这种昆虫传播疟疾与黄热病之后，这个词于 19 世纪后期进入公共卫生词汇。

items.en: Both mosquitoes and mosquitos are accepted plurals; the longer form follows the older English habit of doubling the final consonant before -es.
items.cn: mosquitoes 与 mosquitos 两种复数都被接受；较长的一种沿用英语在 -es 前双写末尾辅音的老习惯。

items.en: Source uncertain (detail and first date): the deeper origin and the exact first citation are not settled, so any pre-Latin form offered here is a reconstruction and competing hypotheses are left side by side.
items.cn: 来源不确定（细节与首见年代）：更深的来源与确切最早书证均无定论，此处给出的拉丁语之前形式属重构形式，并列假说一并保留、不作定论。

note.en: Group one collects words that look or sound close but come from other roots; group two collects the small biting flies people mix up with mosquitoes.
note.cn: 第一组收形近音近但来源不同的词；第二组收人们常与蚊子混淆的小型叮咬蝇类。

entries.definition: Mosque comes from Arabic masjid, a place of prostration; the resemblance to mosquito is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: mosque 来自阿拉伯语 masjid，意为叩拜之处；与 mosquito 的相似纯属偶然。

entries.definition: Miskito names a people and a coast of Central America and is spelled with a k; it is not the insect.
entries.definitionCN: Miskito 指中美洲的一个民族与一片海岸，拼写带 k，不是这种昆虫。

entries.definition: This plural is a spelling variant of mosquitoes, not a different word with a different meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 这个复数只是 mosquitoes 的拼写变体，并非意义不同的另一个词。

entries.definition: The compound names the bed net, so the insect word is working as a modifier rather than as the subject.
entries.definitionCN: 这个复合词指床上用的蚊帐，昆虫词在此作修饰语而非主语。

entries.definition: A gnat is a very small biting fly, often a midge; it bites but does not transmit malaria.
entries.definitionCN: gnat 指极小的叮咬蝇，常为蠓；会叮人但不传播疟疾。

entries.definition: A midge is a minute two-winged fly, some species of which bite in swarms near water.
entries.definitionCN: midge 是极小的双翅目蝇，有些种类在水边成群叮人。

entries.definition: Fly is the general name for the order, of which the mosquito is one family.
entries.definitionCN: fly 是这一目的通称，蚊子只是其中一科。

entries.definition: A flea is a wingless jumping insect that bites; it belongs to a different order entirely.
entries.definitionCN: flea 是无翅跳跃的叮咬昆虫，属于完全不同的目。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Spanish mosca 'fly' plus the diminutive -ito gives mosquito, literally 'little fly'.
normal.cn: 西班牙语 mosca「苍蝇」加指小后缀 -ito 构成 mosquito，字面就是「小苍蝇」。

normal.en: The family runs mosquito, mosquitoes, mosquitos, mosquitofish and mosquitocide.
normal.cn: 词族包括 mosquito、mosquitoes、mosquitos、mosquitofish 与 mosquitocide。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: mosquito net, mosquito coil, mosquito-borne disease.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：蚊帐、蚊香、蚊媒疾病。

normal.en: Only the female bites; males feed on nectar.
normal.cn: 只有雌虫叮咬，雄虫吸食花蜜。

normal.en: The larval stage is the wriggler that hangs at the water surface.
normal.cn: 幼虫期就是倒悬在水面的孑孓。

abstract.en: Picture a needle so fine that the sleeper never feels it enter.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细到睡者完全察觉不到的针。

abstract.en: Picture a whole village sleeping under white gauze, one net per bed.
abstract.cn: 想象整个村子睡在白纱之下，每张床一顶帐。

abstract.en: Picture a hundred small boats stinging a harbour like a swarm.
abstract.cn: 想象上百条小船像虫群一样刺痛一座港口。

examples.en: The mosquito net was treated with insecticide and hung over both beds.
examples.cn: 蚊帐经杀虫剂处理，挂在两张床的上方。

examples.en: Mosquitoes breeding in standing water made the drainage project urgent.
examples.cn: 蚊子在积水中繁殖，使排水工程变得紧迫。

examples.en: A mosquito bite on her wrist swelled into a hard red lump.
examples.cn: 她手腕上的蚊叮肿成了一个硬红的包。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mosquito（莫斯基托）」——在池边「莫」名其妙被叮一口的小虫 → 蚊子

root: 西班牙语/葡萄牙语 mosquito「小苍蝇」= mosca「苍蝇」+ 指小后缀 -ito；mosca 源自拉丁 musca「苍蝇」。拉丁 musca 更早来源不确定，所引印欧形式属重构形式。与 mosque（阿拉伯语 masjid）无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from the biting insect, spread to the swarm, the disease chain, its water-borne young, the gear used against it, small warships, the mark it leaves and the prey it becomes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从叮人的昆虫出发，扩展到虫群、疾病链、水中幼期、对付它的器物、小型舰艇、留下的包以及它作为猎物的一面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle-thin mouthpart breaking the skin while a gauze net hangs above the bed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细如针的口器刺破皮肤，床的上方挂着纱帐。

branches.en: THE BITE: the insect and the itchy mark it leaves are two ends of one act.
branches.cn: 叮咬：昆虫与它留下的痒包是同一动作的两端。

branches.en: THE SWARM: the nuisance and the wriggling young both present the insect in numbers.
branches.cn: 虫群：扰人的成蚊与扭动的幼虫都以数量呈现这种昆虫。

branches.en: TRANSMISSION: the bite becomes a link in a chain between patients.
branches.cn: 传播：叮咬成为病人之间链条上的一环。

branches.en: DEFENCE AND METAPHOR: nets and coils answer the bite, and small fast boats borrow it.
branches.cn: 防护与比喻：蚊帐蚊香回应叮咬，小而快的船借用了它。

branches.en: THE PREY: the name finally marks a food item for a larger hunter.
branches.cn: 猎物：名字最后标出一种更大捕食者的食物。

intro.en: Mosquito is a Spanish diminutive built on a Latin root; its English derivatives are compounds, while the Latin family supplies the technical terms.
intro.cn: mosquito 是在拉丁词根上构成的西班牙语指小词；英语派生词多为复合，技术术语则来自拉丁词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin musca 'fly' gives muscid and musciform in zoology; the Spanish diminutive is the branch that produced the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 musca「苍蝇」在动物学中给出 muscid 与 musciform；产生英语名词的是西班牙语指小这一支。

items.example: A mosquito rests on the shaded wall.
items.exampleCN: 一只蚊子在背阴的墙上停歇。
凡有积水处蚊子就能繁殖。

items.meaning: a net hung over a bed
items.example: The mosquito net kept the room quiet at night.
items.exampleCN: 蚊帐让夜里屋里安静下来。

items.example: A mosquito coil smoked in the corner.

items.meaning: a substance that keeps the insect off
items.example: The mosquito repellent smelled of lemon grass.
items.exampleCN: 驱蚊剂有柠檬草的味道。

items.meaning: a small fish that eats larvae
items.example: Mosquitofish were introduced to clear the ponds.
items.exampleCN: 人们引入食蚊鱼来清理池塘。

items.meaning: a substance that kills the insect
items.example: The spray is a mosquitocide for drains.
items.exampleCN: 这种喷雾是用于排水沟的灭蚊剂。

items.example: A mosquito hawk hovered over the path.
items.exampleCN: 一只蚊鹰在小径上方悬停。

definition_zh: 主要地；大部分；通常；几乎全部
definition_en: for the greatest part of a group or amount; in most cases or most of the time; and almost entirely
core_image: 一只盘子里大半装着米饭，边角只留几样小菜
scene: 傍晚的自助餐厅里，长桌大半已经空了，只有靠窗那几盘菜还被夹得七零八落。By eight the buffet was quiet, and the trays that were mostly empty had been stacked by the door.
sceneCN: 这里是「大半、大部分」（第 1 个义项：指一个整体中的多数部分）；句意为到八点时自助餐区已经安静下来，那些大半空了的托盘被叠在门边。图中可辨识物件：长餐台、成摞的托盘、靠窗的菜盘。

pos.zh: 主要地；大部分；通常；几乎全部

derivatives.zh: 与 mostly 同源的基础词，去掉副词后缀 -ly 即得，义为「最多的；大多数的」
由古英语 eall（全部）与 māst（最多）缩合而成，义为「几乎」，与 most 同源
由古英语 ūt（向外）加 most 构成，义为「最远的；极度的」

senses.title: The greatest share of a group
senses.definition: applying to the greater number of people or things in a group
senses.definitionCN: 适用于一个群体中数量占多数的人或物
senses.example: The guests at the wedding were mostly relatives from her side.
senses.exampleCN: 婚礼上的宾客多半是她这边的亲戚。
senses.why: The word is built on the Old English superlative māst, the greatest share, so its first duty is to report how a whole divides rather than to name a frequency.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在古英语最高级 māst（最大的份额）上，所以它首先管的是「一个整体怎么分」，而不是说事情多久发生一次。

senses.title: In most cases, as a habit
senses.definition: happening on most occasions, though not on every one
senses.definitionCN: 在多数场合都会发生，但并非每一次
senses.example: He mostly takes the early train and reads on the way.
senses.exampleCN: 他通常坐早班车，在路上看书。
senses.why: Once the word could mark the larger part of anything, it could also mark the larger part of a routine, which is how a share of a group turned into a habitual frequency.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词能标出任何事物里较大的那部分，它也就能标出日常习惯里较大的那部分，群体份额就这样长成了习惯性的频率。

senses.title: Nearly the whole of an amount
senses.definition: covering the largest part of a quantity or substance, with only a small remainder
senses.definitionCN: 占去数量或物质的最大部分，只剩下很少一点
senses.example: The bottle in the shed is mostly rainwater.
senses.exampleCN: 棚子里那瓶装的几乎全是雨水。
senses.why: Measuring a substance leaves a visible remainder, so the same superlative sense reads as a near total: the greatest share of a bottle is almost the bottle, and the rest is an exception.
senses.whyCN: 给一样东西计量时总会剩下一小点，于是同一个最高级的意思读成了「接近全部」：一只瓶子里的最大份额就是几乎整瓶，剩下那点只是例外。

intro.en: Mostly is an Old English superlative turned into an adverb: most, the greatest share, plus the ending -ly, which says in what manner a statement holds.
intro.cn: mostly 是古英语最高级加副词词尾构成的词：most 指最大的份额，-ly 表示一句话以什么方式成立。

items.en: Māst was the superlative of micel, great, and it named the greatest amount or the greatest share of a group.
items.cn: māst 是 micel（大的）的最高级，指最大的数量，或一个群体中最大的份额。

items.en: The ending -līce came from līc, body or form, and it turned an adjective into an adverb meaning in the manner of something; in English it settled as -ly.
items.cn: -līce 这个词尾出自 līc（身体、形貌），把形容词变成表示「以……方式」的副词；进入英语后固定为 -ly。

items.en: Middle English joined most and -ly into mostli, an adverb reporting what holds for the greater number of cases.
items.cn: 中古英语把 most 与 -ly 合成 mostli，用作副词，表示对多数情形都成立。

items.en: By the fifteenth century mostly was common in the sense of for the greatest part, and it stood beside almost, which had grown from all and most.
items.cn: 到十五世纪，mostly 已常见，意为「大部分」；它与由 all 与 most 合成的 almost 并列使用。

items.en: Modern English keeps three readings: a share of a group, a habitual frequency, and a near total in amount, and dictionaries list them as separate senses.
items.cn: 现代英语保留三种读法：群体中的份额、习惯性的频率、数量上接近全部；词典把它们分列为不同义项。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the Old English words that share the most element; the near-meaning group collects adverbs of majority and frequency.
note.cn: 形近组收与 most 共用词素的古英语词与英语词；近义组收表示多数与频率的副词。

entries.definition: The greatest amount, or the greater number of a group.
entries.definitionCN: 最大的数量，或一个群体中的多数。

entries.definition: Not quite, but very nearly.
entries.definitionCN: 差一点，但非常接近。

entries.definition: Farthest out, or greatest in degree.
entries.definitionCN: 最远的，或程度最大的。

entries.definition: Ranking first in importance or position.
entries.definitionCN: 在重要性或位置上居首的。

entries.definition: More than anything else, or for the greater part.
entries.definitionCN: 首要地，或大部分情况下。

entries.definition: To a great extent.
entries.definitionCN: 在很大程度上。

entries.definition: In most cases or on most occasions.
entries.definitionCN: 多数情况下，或多数场合。

entries.definition: Above all; mostly but not only.
entries.definitionCN: 首先；主要是，但不只是。

normalIntro.en: The word is one Old English superlative plus one adverbial ending, and everything about it follows from the idea of the greatest share.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是一个古英语最高级加一个副词词尾，它的全部用法都从「最大份额」这个想法里长出来。

normal.en: Most is the superlative of great, so mostly begins with the idea of the greatest share, not with a vague idea of many.
normal.cn: most 是 great 的最高级，所以 mostly 的起点是「最大份额」，而不是笼统的「很多」。

normal.en: -ly comes from an Old English word for body or form, and it turns an adjective into a statement about manner.
normal.cn: -ly 出自古英语里表示身体或形貌的词，它把形容词变成说明「方式」的词。

normal.en: Almost is all plus most, a near total, and it sits beside mostly in the same family of degree words.
normal.cn: almost 是 all 加 most，表示接近全部，它与 mostly 并排站在同一族程度词里。

normal.en: Weather reports say mostly sunny because the forecast covers most of a region and most of a day, not every square metre or every minute.
normal.cn: 天气预报说 mostly sunny，因为预报覆盖的是一个地区的大部分和一天的大部分，而不是每一平方米、每一分钟。

normal.en: Mostly because names the leading reason among several, which is the same share logic applied to causes instead of things.
normal.cn: mostly because 指几个原因里最主要的那个，这正是把「份额」的逻辑从事物挪到了原因。

abstract.en: Picture a plate where rice fills most of the surface and two small side dishes take the corners.
abstract.cn: 想象一只盘子，米饭占去大半个盘面，两样小菜只占边角。

abstract.en: A word for the largest share keeps the minority visible: mostly means not entirely, so the rest is still there.
abstract.cn: 一个表示最大份额的词始终让少数派可见：mostly 意为「并非全部」，剩下的部分仍在。

abstract.en: Because it measures shares rather than absolutes, mostly fits sentences that report, estimate and predict, from weather to polls.
abstract.cn: 因为它衡量的是份额而不是绝对，mostly 特别适合报告、估计和预测的句子，从天气到民调都是。

examples.en: The trays on the counter were mostly empty by eight.
examples.cn: 到八点时，柜台上的托盘大半已经空了。

examples.en: She mostly works from home on Fridays.
examples.cn: 她周五通常在家工作。

examples.en: The report is mostly accurate, with two figures out of date.
examples.cn: 这份报告大体准确，只有两个数字过时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莫斯特里」——大半时间都在忙，只剩一点才歇；记住 mostly 是大半、通常、几乎全部。

root: 古英语 māst（最多的，micel 的最高级）加副词词尾 -līce（后作 -ly）构成 mostli，中古英语起意为「大部分」；同族词有 most、almost、utmost、foremost，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the largest share; the senses divide into a share of a group, a habitual frequency, and a near total in amount.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是最大份额；义项分出群体中的多数、习惯性的频率，以及数量上的接近全部。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plate where one dish covers most of the surface and small portions sit at the edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只盘子，一样菜占去大半，边上只留几小份。

branches.en: a tray with a few crumbs left on it
branches.cn: 只剩几点碎屑的托盘

branches.en: a hall where most seats are taken
branches.cn: 大半座位已坐了人的礼堂

branches.en: the early train taken on every working morning
branches.cn: 每个工作日早晨都坐的那班早车

branches.en: a bottle holding water with a thin layer of oil on top
branches.cn: 瓶里几乎全是水，只浮着一薄层油

branches.en: one adverb covering both how often a thing happens and how much of it there is
branches.cn: 同一个副词，既管事情多久发生一次，也管一样东西占了多少

intro.en: One Old English superlative, one adverbial ending and the English words built from them hold the entry together.
intro.cn: 一个古英语最高级、一个副词词尾，以及由它们构成的英语词，把这个词条撑了起来。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded: mostly belongs to the Old English stock of degree words, and its relatives are Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录：mostly 属于古英语的程度词系统，其亲属词来自日耳曼语。

definition_zh: 母亲；根源；像母亲般照顾
definition_en: a female parent, or the source of something
core_image: 母亲把洗好的校服晾在阳台，衣夹在风里轻轻碰响
scene: 母亲把洗好的校服晾在阳台，衣夹在风里轻轻碰响。My mother cooks on Sundays.

senses.title: A female parent
senses.definition: A female parent
senses.definitionCN: 女性的父母
senses.example: My mother cooks on Sundays.
senses.exampleCN: 我妈妈周日做饭。
senses.why: Old English modor is a Germanic kinship word related to Latin mater; it names the female parent.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 modor 是日耳曼语亲属词，与拉丁语 mater 同源，指女性家长。

senses.title: The source or origin of something
senses.definition: The source or origin of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的来源
senses.example: Necessity is the mother of invention.
senses.exampleCN: 需要是发明之母。
senses.why: Because a mother gives life, the word was extended to anything that brings something else into being.
senses.whyCN: 因为母亲给予生命，这个词就扩展到任何使别的事物诞生的事物。

senses.title: To care for someone like a mother
senses.definition: To care for someone like a mother
senses.definitionCN: 像母亲一样照料
senses.example: She mothers the younger students.
senses.exampleCN: 她像母亲一样照顾低年级学生。
senses.why: The noun became a verb for the care a mother gives, often used of someone protective.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词，指母亲般的照料，常指护着别人的人。

intro.en: The history of mother is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: mother 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Modor named the female parent.
items.cn: 古英语 modor 指女性家长。

senses.title: Change of position
senses.definition: the process of changing position or place over time
senses.definitionCN: 随时间改变位置或处所的过程
senses.example: The motion of the pendulum is regular and easy to time.
senses.exampleCN: 钟摆的运动很规律，容易计时。
senses.why: Latin motio is simply a moving, from movere 'to move'; this is the plainest and oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 motio 就是「移动」，出自 movere「移动」；这是最直白、最古老的义项。

senses.title: A gesture that carries a message
senses.definition: a movement of the hand or head used instead of words to signal something
senses.definitionCN: 代替言语、用来示意的手部或头部动作
senses.example: With a quick motion of his hand, the conductor silenced the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 指挥手一挥，大厅便静了下来。
senses.why: A gesture is a small movement that does the work of a sentence.
senses.whyCN: 手势是一个小动作，却承担了一句话的功能。

senses.title: A proposal put to a meeting
senses.definition: a formal proposal presented at a meeting for discussion and a vote
senses.definitionCN: 在会议上正式提出、供讨论并表决的提议
senses.example: The motion to extend the deadline was carried by nine votes.
senses.exampleCN: 延长截止日期的动议以九票通过。
senses.why: To bring something forward is to move it onto the table; the proposal is the thing set in motion before the room.
senses.whyCN: 把某事提出来，就是把它移到桌面上；提议就是被推到全场面前的东西。

senses.title: A request made to a court
senses.titleCN: 向法庭提出的程序申请
senses.definition: a formal request asking a court to make a ruling or take an action
senses.definitionCN: 请求法庭作出裁定或采取行动正式申请
senses.example: The defence filed a motion to dismiss the charge.
senses.exampleCN: 辩方提交了撤销指控的动议。
senses.why: A court, like an assembly, decides only what is moved before it, so the legal request kept the parliamentary name.
senses.whyCN: 法庭和议会一样，只裁决被推到它面前的事，因此法律申请沿用了议会里的名称。

senses.title: The act of starting a process
senses.definition: the act of setting a plan, process or event going
senses.definitionCN: 使计划、进程或事件开始运转的动作
senses.example: One phone call set the whole rescue in motion.
senses.exampleCN: 一个电话启动了整场救援。
senses.why: The fixed phrase set in motion treats a process as a body that must be pushed before it will move.
senses.whyCN: 「使……启动」这一固定说法把进程当作一具必须先推一把才会动的身体。

senses.title: The running of a machine
senses.definition: the working movement of a machine or mechanism, or its state of running
senses.definitionCN: 机器或机构的运转动作，或其正在运行的状态
senses.example: The old lift was in motion again after the belt was replaced.
senses.exampleCN: 换过皮带后，老电梯又运转起来。
senses.why: A machine is a body whose parts move, so its operation is naturally called motion.
senses.whyCN: 机器是一具有部件在动的身体，因此它的运行自然被叫作 motion。

senses.title: The moving works inside a device
senses.definition: the assembly of moving parts inside a device, especially a clock or watch
senses.definitionCN: 装置内部由运动部件组成的机构，尤指钟表机芯
senses.example: A watchmaker cleaned the motion and oiled each pivot.
senses.exampleCN: 钟表匠清理了机芯，并给每个轴心上了油。
senses.why: Watchmakers named the works by the movement they produce, and the term became the trade word for the whole mechanism.
senses.whyCN: 钟表匠以它所产生的运动来命名这套机构，这个说法后来成了整个机芯的行业词。

senses.title: To signal with the hand
senses.definition: to make a movement of the hand or head as a sign or direction
senses.definitionCN: 用手部或头部的动作作为信号或指引
senses.example: The usher motioned us toward the side door.
senses.exampleCN: 引座员示意我们往侧门走。
senses.why: The noun became a verb: to give a motion with the hand is to motion someone.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：用手给出一个动作，就是向某人示意。

intro.en: Motion comes through Old French from Latin motio, a moving, built on the past-participle stem mot- of movere 'to move'. The proposal sense grows from bringing something forward, not from physical travel.
intro.cn: motion 经古法语来自拉丁 motio「移动」，由 movere「移动、推动」的过去分词词干 mot- 构成。动议义由「把某事提出来、推到面前」引申，并非来自物理位移。

items.en: Movere meant to move, to push away, to set in motion; its past-participle stem mot- is the base of the noun.
items.cn: movere 意为移动、推开、使动起来；它的过去分词词干 mot- 是名词的底子。

items.en: Motio, motionis named a moving or a movement; it is a third-declension noun built on the same stem.
items.cn: motio、motionis 指一次移动或运动；这是由同一词干构成的第三变格法名词。

items.en: Old French motion carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first as movement and soon after as a proposal.
items.cn: 古法语 motion 在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，先指移动，不久也指提议。

items.en: English motion is recorded from the fourteenth century in the plain sense of movement, and in legal use soon afterwards.
items.cn: 英语 motion 自十四世纪有「移动」的直白用法记录，随后不久进入法律语境。

items.en: The sense of a proposal grows from the idea of bringing something forward, a motion made in a room rather than in space.
items.cn: 「提议」义从「把某事提出来」这一想法长出，是在房间里而非空间中做出的动作。

items.en: The first dates of the parliamentary and legal senses are approximate; the noun is well attested from the medieval period.
items.cn: 议会义与法律义的最早记录年代为约数；这个名词在中世纪已有充分记录。

note.en: The first group shares the stem of moving; the second group separates motion from a gesture, a proposal and a trend.
note.cn: 第一组共享「移动」的词干；第二组把 motion 与手势、提议、趋势等相邻说法区分开。

entries.definition: The verb and a common noun for a single act of moving; motion is the more formal noun of the process.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，也作普通名词指一次移动；motion 是更正式、指整个过程的名词。

entries.definition: From mot- plus -ive: the reason that moves a person to act, not the act of moving.
entries.definitionCN: 由「移动」词干加表倾向的词尾构成：推动人去行动的理由，不是移动的动作。

entries.definition: Built on the same stem with an agent ending: the thing that produces movement, as an engine does.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词干加表施动者的词尾：产生运动的东西，如发动机。

entries.definition: Com- 'together' plus motion: a confused rushing about of people, a movement that is noisy.
entries.definitionCN: 表「一起」的拉丁前缀加「移动」：人群慌乱地涌动，一种喧闹的移动。

entries.definition: Not a form of motion and from a different source: it comes from a separate Latin noun for an instant or a weight, and in English it names a point in time rather than a movement.
entries.definitionCN: 不是 motion 的一种形式：它来自另一个拉丁名词，指瞬间或重量；英语中它指时间上的一点，而非移动。

entries.definition: Movement in general, often of a group or a trend; motion is more often a single act or a formal proposal.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指运动，常指一群人的行动或趋势；motion 更常指单次动作或正式动议。

entries.definition: A deliberate movement of the body that communicates; motion can be any movement, gesture is always meaningful.
entries.definitionCN: 有传达作用的身体动作；motion 可以是任何动作，gesture 一定带有意义。

entries.definition: A plan offered for consideration; a motion is a proposal put formally to a meeting.
entries.definitionCN: 提出供考虑的计划；motion 是正式提交会议表决的提议。

entries.definition: The ability to move from place to place, used of animals and vehicles rather than of processes.
entries.definitionCN: 从一处到另一处移动的能力，多用于动物与交通工具，而非抽象过程。

entries.definition: The speed at which something moves; motion names the fact of moving, not how fast.
entries.definitionCN: 移动的快慢；motion 说的是「在动」这件事，不涉及快慢。

normal.cn: 同族词有 motion、motionless、motive、motor、commotion。

normal.en: Law says a motion to dismiss is a formal request, not a physical move.

normal.en: Physics describes motion with velocity and acceleration, two ways of measuring how it changes.
normal.cn: 物理用速度与加速度描述运动，这是衡量它如何变化的两种方式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one push: a body changes place, a hand makes a sign, an idea is pushed before a meeting, a request before a court, a process is started, a machine runs, its works are named, and finally the hand itself becomes a verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「推」展开：身体换位、手做出信号、想法被推到会议前、申请被推到法庭前、进程被启动、机器运转、机芯得名，最后手本身变成动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger pushes a piece from one square to the next, and the piece leaves a trail.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指把棋子从一格推到下一格，棋子拖出一道痕迹。

branches.en: THE PLAIN MOVE: a body changes place, and one small move of the hand carries a message.
branches.cn: 直白的动：身体换位，而手的一个小动作传达信息。

branches.en: BROUGHT BEFORE OTHERS: the same push places a proposal before a meeting or a request before a court.
branches.cn: 推到众人面前：同一个推力把提议放到会议前，或把申请放到法庭前。

branches.en: SET GOING: a process is pushed into motion, and a machine keeps moving once it starts.
branches.cn: 使之启动：进程被推入运动，机器一旦启动便持续运转。

branches.en: THE WORKS: the parts that carry the movement inside a watch take the name of movement itself.
branches.cn: 机芯：钟表内部承担运动的那套部件，直接以「运动」命名。

branches.en: THE VERB: the hand that made the sign becomes the act of motioning.
branches.cn: 动词：做出信号的那只手，变成「示意」这个动作。

intro.en: Motion is a Latin noun of moving, and the stem mot- builds verbs, agents and a whole English family.
intro.cn: motion 是表示「移动」的拉丁名词，词干 mot- 还构成动词、施动者名词与整个英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin movere gives motio and motion, and also motive, motor, commotion and momentum; the ending -tion names an action or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 movere 衍生 motio 与 motion，也衍生 motive、motor、commotion 与 momentum；后缀 -tion 表示动作或结果。

senses.definitionCN: 使人愿意去做某事，尤指通过给其一个目标或动力
senses.example: Good teachers motivate students by making the subject matter feel useful.
senses.exampleCN: 好老师让学生觉得所学有用，从而激励他们。
senses.why: Latin movere meant to set in motion, and this verb was formed on motive, the inner force that starts an action, so motivate is literally to set a person moving from inside.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 movere 意为「使动起来」，这个动词由 motive（启动行动的内心力量）构成，所以 motivate 字面就是把人从内部推动起来。

senses.title: To be the reason behind an action
senses.definition: to be the reason or cause that makes an action, choice or change happen
senses.definitionCN: 成为使某个行动、选择或变化发生的理由或原因
senses.example: A wish to protect his family motivated the long move to another city.
senses.exampleCN: 想保护家人的愿望促成了他搬去另一座城市，成了这次远迁的动机。
senses.why: Once a motive is understood as an inner force, the verb can also point the other way: the force itself motivates the deed, so the wish, not the person, becomes the subject of the sentence.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把 motive 理解为一股内在力量，这个动词也能反过来指：那股力量本身促成了行动，于是句子的主语变成愿望本身，而不是人。

senses.title: To set out reasons for a decision
senses.definition: to give reasons for a decision, proposal or statement, especially in formal writing
senses.definitionCN: 为某个决定、提议或说法给出理由，尤用于正式写作
senses.example: The paper motivates its choice of method in a short opening section.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文在开头一小节里为它的方法选择提供了理由。
senses.why: A motive explains why something was done, so the derived verb took on the academic task of setting those reasons out, and motivate acquired the sense of justify.
senses.whyCN: motive 解释一件事为什么被做，于是由它派生的动词接过了学术写作里「把理由摆出来」的任务，motivate 就多了一层「论证、说明理由」的意思。

intro.en: Motivate is a nineteenth-century English coinage built on motive, which came through French from Latin movere, to move.
intro.cn: motivate 是十九世纪英语用 motive 造出来的词，而 motive 经法语来自拉丁语 movere（移动）。

items.en: Movere meant to move or to set in motion, and it supplied the verb behind motion, motive, motor and promote.
items.cn: movere 意为移动、使动起来，是 motion、motive、motor、promote 这些词背后的动词。

items.en: Its participle motus, a movement, also worked as a noun, and English later used the same stem for both physical motion and a stated reason.
items.cn: 它的分词 motus 意为「运动」，也可作名词；英语后来用同一个词干兼指身体的运动与陈述出来的理由。

items.en: Motivus meant serving to move, and medieval writers applied it to ideas and arguments that move the will rather than the body.
items.cn: motivus 意为「起推动作用的」，中世纪的作者把它用在能打动意志而非移动身体的念头与论据上。

items.en: Old French motif named a motive or a reason, and English borrowed motive in the fifteenth century as a word for what prompts action.
items.cn: 古法语 motif 指动机或理由，英语在十五世纪借入 motive，用来指促使人行动的东西。

items.en: The verb motivate is generally dated to the nineteenth century, when writers on psychology and education added -ate to motive and used it for the act of supplying a reason.
items.cn: 动词 motivate 一般认为形成于十九世纪，研究心理与教育的作者在 motive 后加 -ate，用它表示「提供理由」这件事。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin verb of moving and its English family; the near-meaning group collects verbs for pushing a person toward action or for supplying grounds.
note.cn: 形近组顺着拉丁语「移动」动词及其英语词族展开；近义组收表示推动人行动或提供理由的动词。

entries.definition: A reason that makes someone act in a particular way.
entries.definitionCN: 使人以某种方式行动的理由。

entries.definition: The act or process of moving.
entries.definitionCN: 移动的动作或过程。

entries.definition: To raise someone to a higher position, or to help something advance.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人提到更高职位，或推动某事进展。

entries.definition: A strong feeling that moves a person.
entries.definitionCN: 推动人的强烈情绪。

entries.definition: To give someone confidence or support to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 给某人信心或支持去做某事。

entries.definition: To fill someone with the desire to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人产生做某事的愿望。

entries.definition: To force or push someone into a state or action.
entries.definitionCN: 迫使或推动某人进入某种状态或行动。

entries.definition: To cause someone to do something, often quickly.
entries.definitionCN: 促使某人（往往马上）做某事。

normalIntro.en: The word stands on a Latin verb of moving, and its family keeps returning to the force that starts an action and to the reason given for it afterwards.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词立在拉丁语「移动」动词上，同族词反复回到启动行动的那股力，以及事后为行动给出的理由。

normal.en: Movere is the Latin verb to move, and motive names the force that starts the moving, so motivate is to set a person in motion.
normal.cn: movere 是拉丁语「移动」，motive 指启动移动的那股力，所以 motivate 就是把人推动起来。

normal.en: The ending -ate turns a noun or adjective into a verb of action, which is how motive became motivate in the nineteenth century.
normal.cn: -ate 这个结尾把名词或形容词变成表示动作的动词，motive 就是这样在十九世纪变成了 motivate。

normal.en: Motivation adds -ion and names the force itself, while motivator adds -or and names the person or thing that supplies it.
normal.cn: motivation 加 -ion，指那股力本身；motivator 加 -or，指提供那股力的人或物。

normal.en: De- reverses the verb, so demotivate is to take the drive away, a word that works because motivate is about a force.
normal.cn: de- 把动词反转，所以 demotivate 就是把动力拿走；这个词讲得通，正因为 motivate 说的是一股力。

normal.en: A coach, a teacher and a bonus can all be subjects of motivate, because the word cares about the reason supplied, not about who supplies it.
normal.cn: 教练、老师和奖金都可以做 motivate 的主语，因为这个词在意的是提供了什么理由，而不是谁来提供。

abstract.en: Picture a person standing still until a small light far ahead catches the eye, and the first step follows.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人原本站着不动，直到远处一点亮光吸住目光，第一步就跟着迈了出去。

abstract.en: A motive is invisible, yet it is the hinge on which a whole day of effort turns, so one small reason can move a large body.
abstract.cn: 动机看不见，却是一整天努力转动的那个铰链，所以一个小理由就能挪动一整个人。

abstract.en: To motivate is to hand someone a reason; to be motivated is to take that reason and make it your own.
abstract.cn: 激励是把一个理由交到别人手上；受到激励，则是接过这个理由并把它变成自己的。

examples.en: Good teachers motivate students by making the subject matter feel useful.
examples.cn: 好老师让学生觉得所学有用，从而激励他们。

examples.en: A wish to protect his family motivated the long move to another city.
examples.cn: 想保护家人的愿望促成了他搬去另一座城市。

examples.en: The paper motivates its choice of method in a short opening section.
examples.cn: 这篇论文在开头一小节里为它的方法选择提供了理由。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莫提为特」——莫提一个理由，就为特地去行动；记住 motivate 是激励、成为动机、说明理由。

root: 拉丁语 movere（移动）的过去分词 motus 派生出 motivus（推动的），经法语 motif 与英语 motive 后，十九世纪加 -ate 构成 motivate；同族词有 motive、motion、motor、promote、emotion。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a reason that sets a person moving; the senses divide into supplying that reason, being that reason, and stating reasons in formal prose.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是让人动起来的理由；义项分出提供这股理由、本身成为理由，以及在正式文字里陈述理由。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person standing still until a distant light pulls the first step out of them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人原本停住，远处一点光把他的第一步拉了出来。

branches.en: a coach turning an old story into a reason to run harder
branches.cn: 教练把一段旧事变成一个更拼命跑的理由

branches.en: a bonus that makes a team arrive early
branches.cn: 一笔让团队提前到岗的奖金

branches.en: a wish to protect a family that pulls a household to a new city
branches.cn: 想保护家人的愿望把一家人拉到新城市

branches.en: a paragraph in a paper that sets out why one method was chosen
branches.cn: 论文里交代为何选某种方法的一段

branches.en: one verb for the force behind a deed and for the account given of it
branches.cn: 同一个动词，既指行动背后的力，也指事后给出的说明

intro.en: A Latin verb of moving, its participle, the adjective motivus and a small English family carry the word from physical motion to inner reasons.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语「移动」动词、它的分词、形容词 motivus，再加一小族英语词，把这个词从身体的移动带到内心的理由。

latinIntro.en: Latin movere, motus and motivus form the chain that English motive and motivate rest on.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的 movere、motus 与 motivus 构成一条词链，英语的 motive 与 motivate 就立在它上面。

items.meaning: the force or reason behind action

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或状态的名词词尾

definition_zh: 动机；目的；主题；动力的；推动的
definition_en: the inner force or reason that makes a person act in a certain way; also an adjective meaning causing or supplying motion
core_image: 一只手从背后推着人往某个方向走
scene: 侦探反复追问同一个问题：什么动机能让安静的邻居开三小时车去一栋空屋？The detective kept returning to one question: what motive would make a quiet neighbour drive three hours to an empty house?
sceneCN: 这里 motive 是「作案动机」（第 2 个义项：侦查语境中驱使人行动的内在原因）；句意：探长反复回到同一个问题：什么样的动机会让一个安静的邻居开三小时车去一栋空房子？场景要点：一间堆满卷宗的办公室、一张标着三小时车程的地图、一栋没有人的房子；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 动力的；推动的；引起运动的

collocations.zh: 别有用心；不可告人的动机

derivatives.zh: 激励；促使；成为……的动机
