senses.title: The push from inside
senses.definition: the inner feeling, need, or desire that makes a person choose to act in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 使人选择以某种方式行动的内在感受、需要或欲望
senses.example: Her motive was not money but curiosity.
senses.exampleCN: 她的动机不是钱，而是好奇。
senses.why: Medieval Latin motivus meant 'moving, impelling'. The noun names the moving force inside a person, the push that starts the action before any explanation is given.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪拉丁语 motivus 意为“使移动、推动”。这个名词命名人内部那股推动力，即行动开始、解释尚未给出之前的那一推。

senses.title: A motive in an investigation
senses.definition: the reason a person is believed to have committed a crime or a harmful act
senses.definitionCN: 被认为促使某人实施犯罪或伤害行为的那个原因
senses.example: The police found no motive for the attack.
senses.exampleCN: 警方没有找到这次袭击的动机。
senses.why: Detectives work backwards from an act to the push that could have produced it. In that setting, motive becomes the hidden spring the whole case must locate.
senses.whyCN: 探员从行为倒推，寻找可能产生它的那一推。在这种语境里，动机变成了整个案件必须找到的那根隐藏的发条。

senses.title: A motive kept out of sight
senses.titleCN: 隐藏的、不可告人的动机
senses.definition: a real reason for acting that a person does not admit, often because it is self-interested
senses.definitionCN: 一个人不愿承认的真实动因，常因它出于私利
senses.example: He offered to help, but she suspected an ulterior motive.
senses.exampleCN: 他主动提出帮忙，但她怀疑他别有用心。
senses.why: If a motive is a push, it can be applied from behind, where no one sees it. The phrase 'ulterior motive' places the push out of sight, beyond the stated reason.
senses.whyCN: 如果动机是一推，它就可以从背后施加，让人看不见。“ulterior motive”这一说法把这一推放到视线之外，越过了明面上说出的理由。

senses.title: The profit motive
senses.definition: the desire for financial gain considered as the force that drives investment and business activity
senses.definitionCN: 把对经济收益的渴望看作驱动投资与商业活动的力量
senses.example: The profit motive drives most of the investment in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 利润动机驱动着这个地区的大部分投资。
senses.why: Economics turns the inner push into a system-wide force. When many people are moved by gain, the motive stops being personal and becomes the engine of a market.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把内在的一推变成整个系统的力量。当许多人被收益推动时，动机就不再是个人的，而成了市场的引擎。

senses.title: A motive behind a group act
senses.definition: the stated or suspected force behind a collective decision, such as a reform or a policy
senses.definitionCN: 集体决定背后的、被说明或被怀疑的推动力，如改革或政策
senses.example: The reform was pushed by political motives rather than by evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 推动这项改革的不是证据，而是政治动机。
senses.why: A group can be pushed too. The word then names whatever moves an assembly, party, or institution, even when no single person's feeling is involved.
senses.whyCN: 群体也会被推动。这时这个词命名的是推动一个议会、政党或机构的东西，即使其中并不涉及某一个人的感受。

senses.title: A musical motive
senses.definition: a short recurring figure or theme in a piece of music or art, often carrying a meaning
senses.definitionCN: 音乐或艺术作品中反复出现的短小音型或主题，常带有某种含义
senses.example: The three-note figure returns as a leading motive in the third act.
senses.exampleCN: 那个三音音型在第三幕作为主导动机再次出现。
senses.why: A motive in music is a small unit that keeps moving through the work, returning and developing. It is a push that carries the listener forward, which is why the same word serves both action and art.
senses.whyCN: 音乐中的动机是一个在作品中不断移动、反复出现并发展的短小单位。它是一股推着听者往前的力量，所以同一个词既用于行动，也用于艺术。

senses.title: Motive in law and morality
senses.titleCN: 法律与道德评价中的动机
senses.definition: the reason for an act as judged in law or ethics, especially when it affects how the act is evaluated
senses.definitionCN: 在法律或伦理评判中一个行为的原因，尤当它影响对该行为的评价时
senses.example: The court weighs the motive as well as the act itself.
senses.exampleCN: 法院既衡量行为本身，也衡量其动机。
senses.why: Law cares where the push came from, not only where it ended. A helping hand moved by kindness and one moved by gain produce similar acts but different judgments, so motive becomes a separate thing to assess.
senses.whyCN: 法律关心这一推从何而来，而不只是它把行为推到了哪里。出于善意的手和出于获利的手做出相似的行为，却得到不同的评判，所以动机成了需要单独评估的东西。

senses.title: Motive power
senses.definition: in the adjective use, the force that drives a machine or a process, as in 'motive power'
senses.definitionCN: 形容词用法中指驱动机器或过程的力量，如“motive power”
senses.example: Steam was the motive power of the first factories.
senses.exampleCN: 蒸汽是第一批工厂的动力。
senses.why: The adjective kept the literal Latin sense 'causing motion'. Steam moves an engine exactly as a desire moves a person, so the same word covers both the mental and the mechanical push.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了拉丁语字面的“引起运动”之义。蒸汽推动发动机，正如欲望推动人，所以同一个词同时覆盖心理与机械的推动。

senses.title: Motive force
senses.definition: in technical or literary use, a force that produces movement, as in 'motive force'
senses.definitionCN: 在技术或文学用法中指产生运动的力量，如“motive force”
senses.example: Gravity is the motive force behind the landslide.
senses.exampleCN: 重力是这场滑坡背后的作用力。
senses.why: Here the word is almost physics: whatever makes a body begin to move. The inner push and the physical push are the same picture seen from two sides.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词几乎属于物理学：任何使物体开始运动的东西。内在的一推与物理的一推，是同一幅画面的两面。

intro.en: Motive comes from Medieval Latin motivus 'moving' through French, and the whole family keeps one image: something that sets a body, or a person, in motion. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: motive 经法语来自中世纪拉丁语 motivus“使移动的”，整个词族都保留同一幅画面：某物使一个身体、或一个人开始运动。年代为大致估计。

items.en: The noun first meant 'something brought forward, a proposition, assertion, or argument', a sense now obsolete. It came from Old French motif, a noun use of an adjective literally meaning 'moving'.
items.cn: 名词最初意为“被提出的东西、命题、主张或论点”，这一义项今已废弃。它来自古法语 motif，是字面意为“移动的”形容词的名词化用法。

items.en: Medieval Latin motivus meant 'moving, impelling'. It came from Latin motus 'a moving, motion', the past participle of movere 'to move'.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 motivus 意为“使移动的、推动的”。它来自拉丁语 motus“移动、运动”，即 movere“移动”的过去分词。

items.en: Movere goes back to PIE *meue- 'to push away'. The same root gives motor, emotion, promote, remote, and locomotive.
items.cn: movere 可追溯到原始印欧语 *meue-“推开”。同一词根给出 motor、emotion、promote、remote 与 locomotive。

items.en: The modern sense, 'that which inwardly moves a person to behave a certain way, a mental state or force which induces an action of volition', is recorded from the early fifteenth century. Hence also 'the design or object one has in any action'.
items.cn: 现代义“在内部促使人以某种方式行动的东西，即引发意志行动的心理状态或力量”记录于 15 世纪早期。由此也引申出“任何行动中所抱的目的或对象”。

items.en: The adjective meant 'having control of motion, causing motion, having power to move someone or something'. It survives mainly in fixed phrases such as motive power and motive force.
items.cn: 形容词意为“控制运动的、引起运动的、有能力推动某人或某物的”。它主要存活于 motive power、motive force 这类固定短语中。

items.en: Motive and motivation now divide the work: motive is the inner spring itself, while motivation covers the whole process or supply of drive. Reason is the account offered for an act, and incentive is an external lure. Motivate is the verb built on motive.
items.cn: motive 与 motivation 如今分工：motive 是那根内在的发条本身，motivation 则覆盖整个激励过程或动力的供给。reason 是为行为给出的解释，incentive 是外部的诱因。motivate 是由 motive 构成的动词。

note.en: The first group separates the verb, the process noun, and the adjective built on motive; the second compares the words learners use when they mean 'why someone acted'.
note.cn: 第一组把由 motive 构成的动词、过程名词与形容词分开；第二组比较学习者表达“某人为何行动”时混用的几个词。

entries.definition: to give someone a reason or drive to act. It is the act of supplying the push, while motive is the push itself.
entries.definitionCN: 给某人行动的理由或动力。它是提供这一推的动作，而 motive 是这一推本身。

entries.definition: the whole process of being driven to act, or the amount of drive a person has. It is wider than motive: one motive is a specific spring, motivation is the general force or the study of it.
entries.definitionCN: 被驱动去行动的整个过程，或一个人拥有的动力总量。它比 motive 更宽：一个 motive 是一根具体的发条，motivation 是总体力量或对它的研究。

entries.definition: intended to increase someone's drive, as in a motivational speech. It describes the effect on drive, not the reason for a single act.
entries.definitionCN: 旨在增强某人干劲的，如励志演讲。它描述对干劲的效果，而不是某一次行动的原因。

entries.definition: done without any discernible reason. The -less suffix marks the absence of exactly the inner push that motive names.
entries.definitionCN: 没有任何可辨原因的。 -less 后缀标记的正是 motive 所指那根内在发条的缺席。

entries.definition: the explanation a person gives for an act, or the grounds that make it intelligible. A motive is the inner push; a reason is the account laid out for others, which may or may not match the motive.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人为行为给出的解释，或使该行为可被理解的理由。motive 是内在的一推；reason 是摆给别人看的说法，它未必与动机相符。

entries.definition: something offered from outside, such as a reward, that encourages a person to act. It is the bait in front, while a motive is the push behind.
entries.definitionCN: 从外部提供、鼓励人去行动的东西，如奖励。它是前面的诱饵，而 motive 是背后的推力。

entries.definition: the result or end a person intends to bring about. Purpose looks forward to what the act is for; motive looks back to what started it.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人打算造成的结果或终点。purpose 向前看行为为了什么；motive 向后看是什么启动了行为。

entries.definition: a sudden urge to act, often without deliberation. It is a motive at its most immediate and least reasoned.
entries.definitionCN: 突然的、常未经深思的行动冲动。它是动机最直接、最少经过推理的形态。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin movere 'to move', its participle motus, Medieval Latin motivus, and the English family motor, emotion, and motivate.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 movere“移动”、它的分词 motus、中世纪拉丁语 motivus，以及英语词族 motor、emotion、motivate。

normal.en: movere means 'to move'; motivus means 'moving, impelling'. A motive is the thing that moves a person, seen from inside.
normal.cn: movere 意为“移动”，motivus 意为“使移动的、推动的”。motive 就是从内部看、推动一个人的那个东西。

normal.en: The noun first meant 'a proposition brought forward' in the late 1300s; the inner-drive sense is early 1400s.
normal.cn: 名词在 14 世纪晚期最初意为“被提出的命题”；内在驱动义要到 15 世纪早期。

normal.en: motive, motor, emotion, promote, and locomotive all contain the same 'move' root.
normal.cn: motive、motor、emotion、promote、locomotive 都含有同一个“移动”词根。

normal.en: Motivate is the act of supplying a push; motivation is the whole supply or process; motive is one particular spring.
normal.cn: motivate 是提供一推的动作；motivation 是整体的供给或过程；motive 是某一根具体的发条。

normal.en: A reason is what you say; a motive is what pushed you. The two can differ, which is why detectives distrust stated reasons.
normal.cn: reason 是你说出来的，motive 是推你的那股力。两者可以不一致，所以探员不轻信口头理由。

abstract.en: Picture a hand between someone's shoulder blades, pushing. The person moves forward, but the hand is behind and unseen.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按在某人肩胛之间向前推。人往前走了，而那只手在背后，看不见。

abstract.en: An incentive is a coin held out in front; a motive is the hand behind. A person can be led by either, or by both at once.
abstract.cn: incentive 是举在前面的一个硬币；motive 是背后的那只手。人可能被其中任何一个引导，也可能同时被两者引导。

abstract.en: In music the same push becomes a few notes that keep returning, moving the piece forward each time they sound.
abstract.cn: 在音乐里，同一股推力变成几个不断回来的音符，每次响起都把作品往前推一段。

examples.en: No one could explain the motive behind the anonymous donation.
examples.cn: 没有人能解释这笔匿名捐款背后的动机。

examples.en: The profit motive can build a railway and also abandon a town.
examples.cn: 利润动机可以修起一条铁路，也可以抛下一座城镇。

examples.en: The court found that his motive was fear, not hatred.
examples.cn: 法院认定他的动机是恐惧，而不是仇恨。

dict_mnemonic.text: “莫替吾”——莫替吾拿主意，吾自有推吾向前的那股劲 → motive 动机（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 movere“移动”的派生形式 motivus“使移动的”，核心是“从背后推动人行动的那股力”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of motive, all from one hand pushing from behind: the force may be hidden or admitted, personal or collective, mental or mechanical, but it always sets something in motion.
sensesIntro.cn: motive 的九个义项都来自背后那只推动的手：这股力可以隐藏或明说，可以属于个人或群体，可以是心理的或机械的，但它总使某物开始运动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pushing a person forward from behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手从背后把人向前推。

branches.en: INNER SPRING: the push is felt from inside a person, and in art the same push becomes a recurring figure that moves the work along.
branches.cn: 内在发条：这一推从人的内部被感受到；在艺术中，同一股推力变成反复出现的音型，把作品往前带。

branches.en: HIDDEN AND HUNTED: detectives search for the push behind a crime, and an ulterior motive is the same push kept out of sight.
branches.cn: 隐藏与被追查：探员寻找罪行背后的那一推，而别有用心就是同一推被藏在视线之外。

branches.en: COLLECTIVE FORCES: profit moves a market, and political motives move a reform or a party.
branches.cn: 集体力量：利润推动市场，政治动机推动改革或政党。

branches.en: JUDGMENT: law and ethics ask where the push came from, because origin changes the value of the act.
branches.cn: 评判：法律与伦理追问这一推从何而来，因为来源会改变行为的价值。

branches.en: MECHANICAL PUSH: the adjective keeps the literal sense, naming steam, gravity, or any force that starts motion.
branches.cn: 机械推动：形容词保留字面义，命名蒸汽、重力或任何使运动开始的力量。

intro.en: Motive is a Latin-derived adjective in -ive built on the 'move' stem mot-. The same stem, with e-, pro-, re-, and -or, builds emotion, promote, remote, and motor.
intro.cn: motive 是拉丁语来源、以 -ive 结尾的形容词，词干 mot- 意为“移动”。同一词干加上 e-、pro-、re- 与 -or，构成 emotion、promote、remote 与 motor。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is movere 'to move', with its participle motus and the Medieval Latin adjective motivus. The family is large because 'move' is one of the oldest and most productive ideas in the language.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词基是 movere“移动”，另有其分词 motus 与中世纪拉丁语形容词 motivus。这个词族庞大，因为“移动”是语言中最古老、最能产出的观念之一。

items.meaning: a moving force; an inner reason
items.meaningCN: 推动力；内在动机（mot- 移动 + -ive 形容词或名词后缀）
items.example: The motive for the trip was to see his father.
items.exampleCN: 这趟旅行的动机是去看他父亲。

items.meaning: to supply a reason or drive
items.meaningCN: 激励；促使（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: Good teachers motivate students to ask questions.

items.meaning: the process or strength of being driven
items.meaningCN: 动机；积极性（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: Her motivation fell after the third rejection.
items.exampleCN: 第三次被拒之后，她的积极性下降了。

items.meaningCN: 激励的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: He gives a motivational talk every Monday.
items.exampleCN: 他每周一做一次励志演讲。

items.example: The novel describes a motiveless crime.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说描写了一桩没有动机的罪行。

items.meaning: one who or that which imparts motion
items.meaningCN: 发动机；马达（mot- 移动 + -or 施动者）
items.example: The small motor turns the fan.

items.meaning: a feeling that moves a person
items.meaningCN: 情感；情绪（e- 向外 + motion 运动）
items.example: The speech stirred a strong emotion in the crowd.
items.exampleCN: 这番讲话在人群中激起强烈的情绪。

items.meaning: to move something forward; to advance
items.meaningCN: 促进；提升（pro- 向前 + mot- 移动）
items.exampleCN: 这场活动推广本地农户。

items.meaningCN: 遥远的；偏僻的（re- 向后 + mot- 移动）
items.example: They live in a remote village without a bus.
items.exampleCN: 他们住在一个没有公交的偏远村庄。

items.meaning: a railway engine that moves itself
items.meaningCN: 机车；火车头（loco 从某地 + motive 移动的）
items.example: The old locomotive still runs on weekends.
items.exampleCN: 那台老机车周末仍在运行。

items.meaning: the act of moving, or an organized campaign
items.meaningCN: 移动；运动（-ment 构成名词）
items.example: A slow movement of the crowd began near the gate.
items.exampleCN: 人群在门口附近开始缓慢移动。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 使移动的；推动的（motus 移动 + -ivus 形容词后缀）
移动；运动（movere 的过去分词）

definition_zh: 发动机；马达；汽车；机动的；运动（神经）的
definition_en: a machine that turns energy into movement; a car, in British informal use; and, as an adjective, relating to engine-driven vehicles or to the body's own movement
core_image: 一圈铜线圈在铁壳里旋转，把电变成持续不断的转力
scene: 修车间的木架上放着一台拆开的旧机器，铜线圈露在外面，地上掉着几颗螺丝。A rusty electric motor lay on the bench, its copper coil exposed.
sceneCN: 这里是「电动机、马达」（第 1 个义项：把能量转成转动的机器）；句意为木架上放着一台生锈的电动机，铜线圈露在外面。图中可辨识物件：木架、铜线圈、散落的螺丝。

derivatives.zh: 由 motor 加 -ist 构成，义为「驾车者；开车的人」
由 motor 与 way 复合而成，义为「高速公路」
由 motor 加 -ize 构成，义为「使机动化；给……装上发动机」
由希腊语 autos（自己）与 motive 构成，义为「汽车的；机动车辆的」

senses.title: A machine that turns energy into movement
senses.definition: a machine that uses electricity or fuel to produce movement and drive another machine
senses.definitionCN: 用电或燃料产生运动、驱动另一台机器的装置
senses.example: The fan stopped when its motor burned out.
senses.exampleCN: 风扇的电动机烧坏后就不转了。
senses.why: Latin motor meant a mover, one that sets something else going, and English applied the name to the machine that does exactly that inside another machine.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 motor 意为「推动者」，即让别的东西动起来的那一方；英语把这个名字给了在另一台机器内部干这件事的装置。

senses.title: A car in British speech
senses.definition: a car, especially in informal British English
senses.definitionCN: 汽车，尤用于英式口语
senses.example: They packed the children into the motor and drove north.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把孩子们塞进车里，开车往北去。
senses.why: Once the engine was the interesting part of a vehicle, British speech began calling the whole vehicle a motor, keeping the machine's name for the thing it drove.
senses.whyCN: 当发动机成了一辆车里最要紧的部分，英式口语干脆把整辆车都叫 motor，用机器名代替它所驱动的东西。

senses.title: Belonging to engine-driven vehicles
senses.definition: connected with vehicles that have engines, or with the trade that makes and sells them
senses.definitionCN: 与装有发动机的车辆有关的，或与制造、销售这类车辆的行业有关的
senses.example: The motor trade hired fewer school leavers that year.
senses.exampleCN: 那一年汽车行业招收的毕业生减少了。
senses.why: The noun grew an adjective without changing shape: anything belonging to engine-driven vehicles could take the word as a label, so motor trade and motor vehicle need no suffix.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词没变形就长出了形容词用法：凡属于发动机驱动车辆的事物，直接拿这个词当标签就行，于是 motor trade、motor vehicle 都不必再加词尾。

senses.title: Belonging to the body's movement system
senses.definition: connected with the nerves and muscles that produce movement in the body
senses.definitionCN: 与身体中产生运动的神经和肌肉有关的
senses.example: The injury damaged the motor nerves in his left hand.
senses.exampleCN: 这次受伤损伤了他左手的运动神经。
senses.why: Physiologists needed a word for the body's own movers, the nerves and muscles that carry out a command, and motor was the obvious borrow from mechanics.
senses.whyCN: 生理学家需要给身体里执行指令的推动者——神经与肌肉——一个名字，于是从机械学里直接借来了 motor 这个词。

intro.en: Motor is the Latin agent noun for a mover, taken into English in the nineteenth century and then extended from engines to cars and to the body's nerves.
intro.cn: motor 是拉丁语里表示「推动者」的施动名词，十九世纪进入英语，随后从发动机扩展到汽车与身体的神经。

items.en: Movere meant to move or to set in motion, and it stands behind a large family of English words about movement.
items.cn: movere 意为移动、使动起来，英语里一大族与运动有关的词都出自它。

items.en: Motor was a Latin noun for the mover, the one who or that which sets something in motion, though it was much rarer than the verb beside it.
items.cn: motor 是拉丁语名词，指推动者，即让某物动起来的人或物；不过比起旁边的动词，它出现得要少得多。

items.en: English took motor with the rise of machines driven by steam and electricity, using it first for the source of motion and then for the engine itself.
items.cn: 随着蒸汽与电力驱动的机器兴起，英语借入了 motor，先指运动的来源，再指发动机本身。

items.en: By the early twentieth century British speakers were calling a car a motor, a shortening of motor car, and the word entered everyday speech.
items.cn: 到二十世纪初，英式说法开始把汽车叫作 motor，这是 motor car 的缩短形式，这个词由此进入日常口语。

items.en: Modern English keeps the engine noun, the British car noun, the vehicle adjective, and the physiological adjective for nerves and skills.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了这个名词指发动机、英式口语里指汽车、形容词指车辆，以及生理学上形容神经与技能。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin mover family; the near-meaning group collects words for engines and for the vehicles they drive.
note.cn: 形近组顺着拉丁语「移动」词族展开；近义组收表示发动机以及它所驱动车辆的词。

entries.definition: Movement, or a formal proposal put to a meeting.
entries.definitionCN: 运动；会议上正式提出的动议。

entries.definition: A reason that makes someone act.
entries.definitionCN: 促使人行动的理由。

entries.definition: To raise someone in rank or help something advance.
entries.definitionCN: 提升某人的职位，或推动某事进展。

entries.definition: A strong feeling that moves a person.
entries.definitionCN: 推动人的强烈情绪。

entries.definition: A machine that turns fuel into motion.
entries.definitionCN: 把燃料转成运动的机器。

entries.definition: A machine that produces electricity.
entries.definitionCN: 产生电力的机器。

entries.definition: A road vehicle with four wheels and its own engine.
entries.definitionCN: 自带发动机的四轮道路车辆。

entries.definition: A machine used for carrying people or goods.
entries.definitionCN: 用来运送人或货物的机器。

normalIntro.en: A Latin agent noun runs through the family, so every sense of the word names something that moves other things rather than something that is moved.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拉丁语施动名词贯穿这个词族，所以这个词的每个义项都在给「推动别的东西」的那一方命名，而不是被推动的一方。

normal.en: Movere is the Latin verb to move, and motor is its agent noun, the one that moves, which is why a motor is never the thing moved but the thing that moves others.
normal.cn: movere 是拉丁语「移动」，motor 是它的施动名词，指「推动者」；所以 motor 从来不是被推动的东西，而是推动别的东西的那一方。

normal.en: The -or ending in motor is the same agent ending found in actor and doctor, so the word literally names a doer.
normal.cn: motor 里的 -or 与 actor、doctor 里的施动词尾相同，所以这个词字面上就是在给一个「做事的角色」命名。

normal.en: Motorist adds -ist to motor, a person who uses a motor vehicle, which shows how a machine name turned into a name for its driver.
normal.cn: motorist 在 motor 后加 -ist，指使用机动车的人，可见机器名如何变成了驾驶者的名字。

normal.en: Motorway is motor plus way, a road built for motor traffic, a compound that says exactly what the road is for.
normal.cn: motorway 是 motor 加 way，指为机动车修的路；这个复合词把路的用途说得明明白白。

normal.en: The physiological sense keeps the original meaning best: motor nerves are the body's own movers, the ones that carry out a command.
normal.cn: 生理学义最贴近原意：运动神经就是身体自己的推动者，负责把指令执行下去。

abstract.en: Picture a coil spinning inside an iron shell, turning current into a steady push.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈线圈在铁壳里旋转，把电流变成一股持续的推力。

abstract.en: A word that names the mover rather than the movement shows how English labels a machine by its role, not by its shape.
abstract.cn: 一个为「推动者」而不是「运动」命名的词，说明英语常按角色给机器命名，而不是按外形。

abstract.en: The same noun reaches from a factory engine to the nerves in a hand, because both are places where a command becomes motion.
abstract.cn: 同一个名词从工厂里的发动机一直伸到手上的神经，因为这两处都是「指令变成运动」的地方。

examples.en: The fan stopped when its motor burned out.
examples.cn: 风扇的电动机烧坏后就不转了。

examples.en: They packed the children into the motor and drove north.
examples.cn: 他们把孩子们塞进车里，开车往北去。

examples.en: The injury damaged the motor nerves in his left hand.
examples.cn: 这次受伤损伤了他左手的运动神经。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摩托」——摩托车里的摩托就是 motor 的音译，本指推动的那台机器；记住 motor 是发动机，也指汽车。

root: 拉丁语 movere（移动）的施动名词 motor（推动者）进入英语，十九世纪起指发动机，二十世纪英式口语又指汽车；同族词有 motion、motive、promote、emotion。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the thing that sets something else moving; the senses divide into the engine, the British car, the vehicle adjective, and the body's own movers.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「让别的东西动起来的那一方」；义项分出机器、英式口语的汽车、车辆的形容词用法，以及身体自己的推动者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a copper coil spinning inside an iron shell and turning current into a steady push.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈铜线在铁壳里旋转，把电流变成持续的推力。

branches.en: a coil spinning inside a rusted casing
branches.cn: 生锈外壳里旋转的一圈线圈

branches.en: a fan blade turning in a hot room
branches.cn: 热房间里转动的风扇叶

branches.en: children bundled into a small car on a cold morning
branches.cn: 冷天早晨被塞进一辆小车的孩子

branches.en: a factory gate where new cars roll out
branches.cn: 新车驶出的工厂大门

branches.en: a hand opening slowly after a nerve signal arrives
branches.cn: 接到神经信号后慢慢张开的手

intro.en: A Latin agent noun, the verb behind it, and a few English suffixes carry motor from a mover to engines, cars and nerves.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语施动名词、它背后的动词，以及几个英语词尾，把 motor 从「推动者」带到发动机、汽车与神经。

latinIntro.en: Latin movere and its agent noun motor supply the whole family, while motus and motivus show the movement and the force that causes it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的 movere 及其施动名词 motor 支撑起整个词族，motus 与 motivus 则分别表示运动与引起运动的力量。

items.meaning: a car driven by an engine
a driver of a motor vehicle

definition_zh: 摩托车；轻便摩托车；机动自行车
definition_en: a two-wheeled vehicle powered by an engine, especially a light one; also a bicycle fitted with a small engine
core_image: 一辆两轮车靠在墙边，座垫上扣着一顶旧头盔
scene: 雨后的巷口，一辆两轮小车贴墙停着，座位被雨水打得发亮。He left his motorbike by the wall and wiped the seat with a cloth.
sceneCN: 这里是「摩托车」（第 1 个义项：以发动机驱动的两轮车）；句意为他把摩托车停在墙边，用布擦了擦座垫。图中可辨识物件：两轮车、墙壁、湿漉漉的座垫。

pos.zh: 摩托车；轻便摩托车；机动自行车

derivatives.zh: 由 motorcycle 加 -ist 构成，义为「摩托车手」
由 motorcycle 加 -ing 构成，义为「摩托车骑行；摩托车运动」
由 bike 加 -er 构成，义为「骑摩托车的人」

senses.title: A two-wheeled machine driven by an engine
senses.definition: a road vehicle with two wheels and an engine, ridden by one or two people
senses.definitionCN: 装有发动机、由一两个人骑乘的两轮道路车辆
senses.example: He left his motorbike by the wall and wiped the seat with a cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 他把摩托车停在墙边，用布擦了擦座垫。
senses.why: The word is a plain compound of motor and bike, so it names the thing by its two parts: an engine plus a bicycle frame.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 motor 与 bike 直接复合而成，所以它用两个部件给东西命名：一台发动机加一副自行车车架。

senses.title: A light motorcycle for short trips
senses.definition: a small, light motorcycle, the kind often used for short journeys in town
senses.definitionCN: 车身轻、排量小的摩托车，多用于城里短途出行
senses.example: She bought a small motorbike for the two-mile ride to the station.
senses.exampleCN: 她买了一辆轻便摩托车，用来骑到两英里外的车站。
senses.why: Because the compound says nothing about size, British speakers use it most often for the small machines that replace a bicycle, and the light sense grew from that habit rather than from the word's form.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个复合词本身不交代大小，英式说法最常拿它指替代自行车的那种小机器，「轻便」这一层意思是从用法习惯里长出来的，而不是词形自带。

senses.title: A bicycle with a small engine added
senses.definition: a bicycle to which a small engine has been fitted, common where fuel is cheap and distances are short
senses.definitionCN: 在自行车上加装小发动机的两轮车，在油价便宜、路途很短的地方常见
senses.example: In the village, a motorbike with pedals was cheaper than a car.
senses.exampleCN: 在村里，一辆带脚踏的机动自行车比汽车便宜。
senses.why: Bike itself means bicycle, so the compound can still be read literally: a bicycle with a motor attached, a reading that survives where such machines are everyday transport.
senses.whyCN: bike 本身是自行车的简称，所以这个复合词仍可照字面读成「装了发动机的自行车」；在那种机器就是日常交通工具的地方，这个读法一直活着。

intro.en: Motorbike joins two ordinary English nouns, motor and bike, and the compound is generally dated to the late nineteenth century, when engine-driven two-wheelers appeared.
intro.cn: motorbike 把 motor 与 bike 两个普通英语名词合在一起，一般认为这个复合词出现于十九世纪后期，正当发动机驱动的两轮车登场。

items.en: The first half goes back to Latin motor, a mover, by way of the English noun motor, the engine that drives a machine.
items.cn: 前半部分可追到拉丁语 motor（推动者），再经英语名词 motor（驱动机器的发动机）而来。

items.en: Bike is a nineteenth-century shortening of bicycle, coined when the pedal-driven two-wheeler became common.
items.cn: bike 是十九世纪 bicycle 的缩略，在脚踏驱动的两轮车普及之时造出。

items.en: Motor and bike were joined as motorbike in the late nineteenth century, a step generally taken to follow the arrival of engine-driven two-wheelers.
items.cn: motor 与 bike 在十九世纪后期合成 motorbike，一般认为这一步跟随发动机驱动两轮车的出现。

items.en: British English adopted motorbike as its everyday word for a motorcycle, while American English usually keeps the longer motorcycle.
items.cn: 英式英语把 motorbike 收作摩托车的日常说法，而美式英语通常仍用较长的 motorcycle。

items.en: Modern English also applies the word to bicycles fitted with small engines, so it now covers both the road machine and the assisted bicycle.
items.cn: 现代英语也用它指加装小发动机的自行车，这个词如今同时涵盖公路上的摩托车与助力自行车。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the two halves of the compound and the vehicles built on them; the near-meaning group collects the two-wheeled machines it is often compared with.
note.cn: 形近组顺着复合词的两个部件以及由它们构成的车辆展开；近义组收常与它比较的两轮车。

entries.definition: A two-wheeled vehicle with an engine, the full form of motorbike.
entries.definitionCN: 装有发动机的两轮车，是 motorbike 的完整说法。

entries.definition: The engine that drives a machine.
entries.definitionCN: 驱动机器的发动机。

entries.definition: A bicycle, or a motorcycle in informal speech.
entries.definitionCN: 自行车，口语里也可指摩托车。

entries.definition: A two-wheeled vehicle moved by pedals.
entries.definitionCN: 靠脚踏驱动的两轮车。

entries.definition: A light two-wheeled vehicle with a small engine and pedals.
entries.definitionCN: 装小发动机、带脚踏的轻型两轮车。

entries.definition: A two-wheeled vehicle with a small engine and a step-through frame.
entries.definitionCN: 装小发动机、车架可以跨步上下的一种两轮车。

entries.definition: A bicycle with an electric motor.
entries.definitionCN: 装有电动机的自行车。

normalIntro.en: Two everyday nouns sit inside this compound, and the family that surrounds it keeps naming the machine, its rider and the activity of riding it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个复合词里装着两个日常名词，围绕它的词族则不断给机器、骑车人和骑车这件事命名。

normal.en: Motor supplies the engine half and bike the frame half, so the compound is a description as much as a name.
normal.cn: motor 提供发动机这一半，bike 提供车架这一半，所以这个复合词既是名字，也是一句描述。

normal.en: Bike is a shortening of bicycle, which is bi- for two plus the Greek word for wheel, so the second half literally says two wheels.
normal.cn: bike 是 bicycle 的缩略，而 bicycle 是 bi-（二）加希腊语「轮子」，所以后半部分字面上就在说「两个轮子」。

normal.en: Motorcycle is the longer, more formal twin, and it is the usual word in American English where motorbike sounds distinctly British.
normal.cn: motorcycle 是更长、更正式的那个对应词，在美式英语里通常用它，而 motorbike 听起来明显是英式说法。

normal.en: Motorist and motorcyclist both add a person suffix to the machine name, turning a vehicle into a word for its rider.
normal.cn: motorist 与 motorcyclist 都在机器名后加表示人的词尾，把车辆变成骑车人的说法。

normal.en: The same word covers the road motorcycle and the assisted bicycle because bike keeps its bicycle sense inside the compound.
normal.cn: 同一个词既指公路上的摩托车，也指助力自行车，因为 bike 在复合词里保留着「自行车」那一层意思。

abstract.en: Picture a bicycle frame with a small engine bolted into the middle, a machine that is half pedal and half piston.
abstract.cn: 想象一副自行车车架，中间焊上一台小发动机，一半是脚踏，一半是活塞。

abstract.en: A compound that simply stacks two everyday words shows that English often names a new machine by naming the old ones it joins.
abstract.cn: 一个把两个日常词叠起来的复合词说明，英语常用「把被合并的两样旧东西说出来」的方式给新机器命名。

abstract.en: The British preference for the short word and the American preference for the long one is a reminder that vocabulary carries address as well as meaning.
abstract.cn: 英式偏爱短词、美式偏爱长词，这提醒人：词汇不只携带意义，也携带口音里的地域。

examples.en: He left his motorbike by the wall and wiped the seat with a cloth.
examples.cn: 他把摩托车停在墙边，用布擦了擦座垫。

examples.en: She bought a small motorbike for the two-mile ride to the station.
examples.cn: 她买了一辆轻便摩托车，用来骑到两英里外的车站。

examples.en: In the village, a motorbike with pedals was cheaper than a car.
examples.cn: 在村里，一辆带脚踏的机动自行车比汽车便宜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摩托拜克」——摩托加拜克，一台发动机架在两个轮子上；记住 motorbike 是摩托车。

root: 由 motor（发动机，源自拉丁语 motor「推动者」）与 bike（bicycle 的缩略）复合而成，一般认为十九世纪后期出现；英式英语常用它指摩托车；同族词有 motorcycle、motorcyclist、biker。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an engine on a bicycle frame; the senses divide into the general road machine, the light town machine, and the pedal bicycle with a small engine.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是把发动机架在自行车车架上；义项分出泛指的公路摩托车、城里的轻便车，以及加装小发动机的脚踏自行车。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bicycle frame with a small engine bolted into the middle, half pedal and half piston.
core.cn: 核心意象：一副自行车车架中间焊上一台小发动机，一半脚踏，一半活塞。

branches.en: a two-wheeled machine leaning against a wet wall
branches.cn: 靠在一堵湿墙上的两轮车

branches.en: a rider pulling on a helmet at the kerb
branches.cn: 在路边拉上头盔的骑手

branches.en: a small machine threading through narrow town streets
branches.cn: 在窄街里穿行的小车

branches.en: a bicycle with an engine bolted under the crossbar
branches.cn: 横梁下焊着发动机的一辆自行车

branches.en: one word for the town runabout and the assisted bicycle
branches.cn: 同一个词，既指城里的轻便车，也指助力自行车

intro.en: Two everyday nouns, their Latin and Greek roots, and a handful of English suffixes make up the entry.
intro.cn: 两个日常名词、它们在拉丁语与希腊语里的根，以及几个英语词尾，构成了这个词条。

latinIntro.en: The first half has a reliable Latin source in motor, a mover; the second half comes from Greek kyklos, wheel, by way of bicycle.
latinIntro.cn: 前半部分有可靠的拉丁语来源 motor（推动者）；后半部分则经 bicycle 来自希腊语 kyklos（轮子）。

items.meaning: an engine that drives a machine
the activity of riding a motorbike

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或活动的词尾

definition_zh: 摩托车；骑摩托车；（作定语）摩托车的
definition_en: a road vehicle with two wheels and an engine that one or two people ride; also used before a noun for equipment, races or police work connected with such vehicles; and as a verb meaning to travel on one
core_image: 两个轮子夹着一台发动机，排气管在暮色里吐出一缕白烟
scene: 黄昏的海岸路上，年轻人把头盔扣紧，发动机的声音压过了风声。He rode his motorcycle along the cliffs until the last light faded.
sceneCN: 这里「motorcycle」是「摩托车」（第 1 个义项：有发动机的两轮车）；句意为他骑着摩托车沿悬崖一路走，直到最后一点光也暗下去。画面里能想见：扣紧的头盔、海岸公路与崖边的暮色。

collocations.zh: 骑摩托的警察；摩托警队

derivatives.zh: 由 motorcycle 去掉词尾再加 -ist 构成，义为「骑摩托车的人」
由 motorcycle 去掉词尾再加 -ing 构成，义为「摩托车运动；骑摩托车」
由 motor 与 bike 缩合而成，义为「摩托车」，与 motorcycle 近义
由 motor 加 -cade（借自 cavalcade 的词尾）构成，义为「机动车辆组成的车队」

senses.title: A two-wheeled vehicle powered by an engine
senses.definition: a road vehicle with two wheels and an engine that one or two people ride
senses.definitionCN: 一种有两个轮子、由发动机驱动的路上交通工具，可载一两个人
senses.example: She parked her motorcycle under the mango tree.
senses.exampleCN: 她把摩托车停在芒果树下。
senses.why: The word is a plain English compound: motor supplies the engine and cycle supplies the wheel, so the name simply describes the machine's two working parts.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是直白的英语复合词：motor 提供发动机，cycle 提供轮子，名字本身就在描述这台机器的两个工作部件。

senses.title: Used before a noun for things connected with motorcycles
senses.titleCN: （作定语）摩托车的；供摩托车使用的
senses.definition: placed before another noun to describe equipment, clothing, races or police work that belongs to motorcycles
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一个名词前，说明某装备、服装、赛事或警务与摩托车有关
senses.example: A row of motorcycle police waited at the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 一队骑摩托的警察在桥边等着。
senses.why: A common noun that names a vehicle easily becomes a label for everything built around it, so helmets, races and patrols simply borrow the vehicle's name.
senses.whyCN: 一个指交通工具的普通名词，很容易变成围绕它的一切事物的标签，于是头盔、比赛和巡逻都直接借用了这辆车的名字。

senses.title: To ride a motorcycle
senses.definition: to travel on a motorcycle, usually as the person steering it
senses.definitionCN: 骑摩托车出行，通常指掌握车把的那个人
senses.example: They motorcycled across the island in three days.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用三天时间骑摩托环游了这座岛。
senses.why: English often turns a vehicle noun into a verb without adding any ending, so the machine's name also names the act of using it.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把一个交通工具名词原样变成动词，于是这台机器的名字同时也指使用它的那个动作。

intro.en: Motorcycle is not a Latin word but a nineteenth-century English compound of two borrowed parts, one for motion and one for the wheel.
intro.cn: motorcycle 不是拉丁词，而是十九世纪英语用两个借来的成分拼成的复合词：一个表示运动，一个表示轮子。

items.en: Kyklos meant a circle or a wheel, and Greek writers used it for anything round, including the wheel of a cart.
items.cn: kyklos 意为圆或轮子，古希腊作家用它指一切圆形之物，包括马车的车轮。

items.en: Latin borrowed kyklos as cyclus and passed the wheel idea into learned English through French forms of cycle.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 kyklos 作 cyclus，又把「轮子」的观念经法语中的 cycle 形式带入学术英语。

items.en: Movere meant to move; its derived noun motor named the thing that gives motion, a term later applied to an engine.
items.cn: movere 意为移动；由它派生的名词 motor 指「使动者」，后来用来指发动机。

items.en: Late nineteenth-century English joined motor and cycle to name engine-driven two-wheelers, at first often written as two words.
items.cn: 十九世纪晚期英语把 motor 与 cycle 合起来指发动机驱动的两轮车，起初常分写成两个词。

items.en: Modern English spells the compound as one word and extends it to motorcycle police, motorcycle racing and the verb to motorcycle.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个复合词连写成一个词，并扩展到摩托警队、摩托车比赛以及动词「骑摩托车」。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the two halves of the compound and words built on them; the near-meaning group gathers small powered two-wheelers.
note.cn: 形近组沿着这个复合词的两半以及建立在它们之上的词展开；近义组收表示小型动力两轮车的词。

entries.definition: The half of the word that supplies the engine and the idea of motion.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词中提供发动机与运动观念的那一半。

entries.definition: A person who drives a car, built on the same motor stem.
entries.definitionCN: 开车的人，建立在同一个 motor 词干上。

entries.definition: The wheel word inside motorcycle, also used for bicycles and repeated rounds.
entries.definitionCN: motorcycle 里表示轮子的那个词，也用于自行车与循环。

entries.definition: A procession of motor vehicles, from motor plus the ending of cavalcade.
entries.definitionCN: 由机动车辆组成的车队，由 motor 加 cavalcade 的词尾构成。

entries.definition: A two-wheeled vehicle driven by pedals, sharing the cycle part.
entries.definitionCN: 靠脚踏驱动的两轮车，与 motorcycle 共用 cycle 这一部分。

entries.definition: A motorcycle, especially a small or light one, in informal British use.
entries.definitionCN: 摩托车，尤指小型轻便的，英式口语用法。

entries.definition: A small motorcycle with a frame you can step through.
entries.definitionCN: 车架可跨步上下的小型摩托车；踏板车。

entries.definition: A light two-wheeled vehicle with a small engine and pedals.
entries.definitionCN: 装有小型发动机和脚踏板的轻型两轮车。

entries.definition: A bicycle or, informally, a motorcycle.
entries.definitionCN: 自行车，口语中也指摩托车。

normalIntro.en: The word is a compound with a moving half and a wheel half, and its family keeps circling engines, riders and the roads they use.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由「动力」与「轮子」两半合成，词族反复围着发动机、骑手和他们走的路转。

normal.en: Motor is the moving part of the name and cycle is the wheel part, so the compound reads almost like a label fixed to the machine.
normal.cn: motor 是名字里「动力」的部分，cycle 是「轮子」的部分，这个复合词读起来几乎像贴在机器上的标签。

normal.en: Motorcyclist swaps the final -e for -ist, the way a person who does something often takes that ending.
normal.cn: motorcyclist 把词尾的 -e 换成 -ist，就像做某事的人常用这个后缀来称呼自己。

normal.en: Motorcycling adds -ing: the activity built around the vehicle.
normal.cn: motorcycling 加 -ing：围绕这辆车展开的活动。

normal.en: Bicycle already joins bi- (two) with cycle, so motorcycle uses the same wheel word with a different first half.
normal.cn: bicycle 已经把 bi-（两个）和 cycle 连在一起，所以 motorcycle 用的是同一个「轮」词，只换了前半截。

normal.en: The noun also works as a verb without any ending, as in 「they motorcycled across the island」.
normal.cn: 这个名词不加词尾也能当动词用，例如「他们骑摩托环游全岛」。

abstract.en: A name made of two borrowed parts reminds us that new machines are often labelled with old words for motion and wheels.
abstract.cn: 由两个借来的成分拼成的名字提醒人：新机器常常用表示运动与轮子的旧词来命名。

abstract.en: The same noun can name the vehicle, its accessories and the ride, because English lets a thing's name spread to everything around it.
abstract.cn: 同一个名词可以指车、指配件、也指骑行本身，因为英语允许一件东西的名字蔓延到它周围的一切。

abstract.en: Two wheels and an engine turn a person into a rider, and the word carries that small transformation inside it.
abstract.cn: 两个轮子加一台发动机，把人变成骑手，而这个词把这场小小的转变装在里面。

examples.en: He rode his motorcycle along the cliffs until the last light faded.
examples.cn: 他骑着摩托车沿悬崖一路走，直到最后一点光也暗下去。

examples.en: A row of motorcycle police waited at the bridge.
examples.cn: 一队骑摩托的警察在桥边等着。

examples.en: She saved for two years before buying her first motorcycle.
examples.cn: 她攒了两年的钱，才买下第一辆摩托车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摩托」——汉语把 motor 音译成「摩托」，再加两个轮子，就是摩托车。

root: motorcycle 是十九世纪英语的复合词，由 motor（源自拉丁语 movere，意为「移动」）与 cycle（源自希腊语 kyklos，意为「圆、轮」）拼合而成，整词层面没有拉丁同族。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an engine joined to two wheels; the senses name the machine itself, its attributive use as a label, and the act of riding it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一台发动机接上两个轮子；义项分别指这台机器本身、它作定语的标签用法，以及骑它的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two wheels with an engine between them, a thin trail of smoke in the dusk.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个轮子中间夹一台发动机，暮色里拖出一缕细烟。

branches.en: a rider tightening a helmet strap at dusk
branches.cn: 暮色中骑手扣紧头盔带子

branches.en: a row of police machines waiting at a bridge
branches.cn: 桥边排开的警用摩托

branches.en: a race banner stretched over a coastal road
branches.cn: 横跨海岸公路的比赛横幅

branches.en: a machine leaning into a long bend
branches.cn: 一辆在长弯里倾斜而过的摩托

branches.en: a tank filled at a roadside station
branches.cn: 在路边加油站加满油

intro.en: Two borrowed halves, an engine word and a wheel word, are held together by English compounding and a handful of endings.
intro.cn: 两个借来的成分——一个引擎词和一个轮子词——由英语复合构词法和几个词尾连接在一起。

latinIntro.en: Movere, motor and cyclus are recorded Latin forms and they supply the two halves of the compound.
latinIntro.cn: movere、motor 与 cyclus 是有记录的拉丁词形，为这个复合词的两半提供来源。

items.meaning: one who or that which does

latinEntries.meaning: a mover, one that imparts motion

definition_zh: 模具；模子；霉；霉菌；塑造；使成形
definition_en: a hollow container that gives shape to soft material; a soft fungus that grows on damp food or surfaces; to press material into a shape, or to influence how a person develops
core_image: 木框里压满湿泥，倒扣在案板上，一只碗的形状脱了出来
scene: 陶艺课的窗边，师傅把湿泥一点点按进木框，再倒扣在木板上。She pressed the clay into a wooden mould and left it near the window to dry.
sceneCN: 这里「mould」是「模具、模子」（第 1 个义项：让软材料成形的凹型容器）；句意为她把陶土按进木模具，放在窗边晾干。画面里能想见：木框、湿泥与倒扣出来的碗坯。

collocations.zh: 按照……的模式；带有……的风格

derivatives.zh: 由 mould 加 -ing 构成，义为「模制品；建筑线脚」
由 mould 加 -y 构成，义为「发霉的；有霉味的」
由 mould 加 -able 构成，义为「可塑的；容易成形的」
由 mould 加 -er 构成，义为「制模工；模塑工」

senses.title: A hollow container that gives a shape to soft material
senses.definition: a hollow container with a particular shape, into which soft material is pressed so that it takes that shape
senses.definitionCN: 具有特定形状的空心容器，把软材料压进去，材料就随之成型
senses.example: She pressed the clay into a wooden mould and left it near the window to dry.
senses.exampleCN: 她把陶土按进木模具，放在窗边晾干。
senses.why: The shaping word goes back to Latin modulus, a small measure; a mould is a measured hollow, so its size is settled before any material enters.
senses.whyCN: 表示「成形」的那个词可追到拉丁语 modulus（小尺度）；模子正是一个量好的空腔，材料还没进去，成品的尺寸就已经定死。

senses.title: A soft fungus growing on damp food or surfaces
senses.definition: a green, grey or white growth of fungus that appears on old food, damp walls or leather
senses.definitionCN: 长在陈旧食物、潮湿墙面或皮革上的灰绿、灰白软质真菌
senses.example: There was grey mould along the bathroom tiles.
senses.exampleCN: 浴室瓷砖的缝隙里长着灰霉。
senses.why: This sense is a different word that shares the spelling; it usually grows where things stay damp and begin to break down, and dictionaries keep it apart from the shaping word.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项是共用同一拼写的另一个词；它总长在潮湿、开始腐烂的东西上，词典把它与表示成形的那个词分开处理。

senses.title: To press a soft material into a shape
senses.definition: to press clay, dough or another soft substance into a particular shape, by hand or in a container
senses.definitionCN: 用手或容器把陶土、面团等柔软物质压成某个形状
senses.example: He moulded the wet sand into a tiny castle.
senses.exampleCN: 他把湿沙子塑成一座小城堡。
senses.why: If the noun is the measured cavity, the verb is the act of filling it; the word moves from the tool to the work done with the tool.
senses.whyCN: 如果名词是那个量好的空腔，动词就是往里填的动作；词于是从工具转到用工具做的那件事。

senses.title: To shape a person's character or beliefs
senses.definition: to influence strongly how someone's character, habits or beliefs develop over time
senses.definitionCN: 强烈影响某人的性格、习惯或信念在长期中如何发展
senses.example: Years of reading moulded her into a patient observer.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的阅读把她塑造成一个有耐心的观察者。
senses.why: A child is soft material in the hands of family and teachers, so the same verb for pressing clay into a mould is used for forming a mind.
senses.whyCN: 孩子在家和老师手里就是软的材料，于是那个「把泥按进模子」的动词被借来形容心智的形成。

intro.en: Mould has two separate histories: the shaping word runs back to a Latin measure, while the fungus word has its own uncertain origin.
intro.cn: mould 有两段各自独立的来历：表示「成形」的词可追到拉丁语的尺度，表示「霉」的词另有来源，确切来历不确定。

items.en: Modulus meant a small measure, a diminutive of modus, and it named the fixed size against which things were checked.
items.cn: modulus 意为「小尺度」，是 modus 的指小形式，指用来核对事物的既定尺寸。

items.en: Old French modle took the word as a pattern or model, the shape a finished object should follow.
items.cn: 古法语把词写作 modle，指样板或模型，即成品应当照着做的形状。

items.en: Middle English used mold for the hollow pattern that potters and metal workers filled with their material.
items.cn: 中古英语用 mold 指陶工与金属工匠往里填料的空心模范。

items.en: The fungus sense is a separate word of uncertain origin; it is often linked to Scandinavian words for mildew and was influenced by the old earth word.
items.cn: 表示霉的义项是另一个来源不确定的词，一般认为与斯堪的纳维亚语中表示霉的词有关，并受到表示泥土的古词影响。

items.en: Modern English keeps British mould and American mold, and adds the verb senses of shaping material and shaping a mind.
items.cn: 现代英语保留英式 mould 与美式 mold 两种拼写，并发展出塑造材料与塑造心智的动词义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the British and American spellings and the shaping family; the near-meaning group gathers words for casting, forming and fungus.
note.cn: 形近组收英式与美式拼写以及「成形」词族；近义组收表示浇铸、成形与真菌的词。

entries.definition: The American spelling of mould, used for the container, the fungus and the verb.
entries.definitionCN: mould 的美式拼写，容器、霉与动词都用它。

entries.definition: Something made in a mould, or a shaped strip along a wall.
entries.definitionCN: 在模子里做出来的东西，或墙面上成形的线脚。

entries.definition: Covered with mould or smelling of damp.
entries.definitionCN: 长满霉的；带着潮味的。

entries.definition: Soft enough to be pressed into a shape.
entries.definitionCN: 软到可以被压成形的。

entries.definition: A small measure in Latin, the source of mould and of module.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中的「小尺度」，是 mould 与 module 的来源。

entries.definition: To pour melted metal or another liquid material into a mould.
entries.definitionCN: 把熔化的金属等液体材料浇进模子。

entries.definition: To give something a particular form.
entries.definitionCN: 给某物一个特定的形状。

entries.definition: To make or develop into a particular shape or arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 使成为或发展成某种形状、结构。

entries.definition: A plant-like growth such as mould, mildew or mushroom.
entries.definitionCN: 霉、白粉病或蘑菇一类近似植物的生长物。

normalIntro.en: One spelling carries a family about measured cavities and a separate word about damp growth; keeping the two apart makes the senses easier to hold.
normalIntro.cn: 同一个拼写承载着「量好的空腔」这一词族，也承载着另一个表示潮湿生长的词；把两者分开，义项就好记了。

normal.en: Modulus is Latin for a small measure, so a mould is a cavity whose size was decided in advance.
normal.cn: modulus 是拉丁语的「小尺度」，所以模子就是尺寸事先定好的空腔。

normal.en: Moulding adds -ing: the object that comes out of the mould, or the shaped strip on a wall.
normal.cn: moulding 加 -ing：从模子里出来的物件，或墙上成形的线脚。

normal.en: Mouldy adds -y: full of mould, therefore spoiled and damp.
normal.cn: mouldy 加 -y：长满霉，因此坏了、带着潮气。

normal.en: Mouldable adds -able: able to take a shape, like wet clay.
normal.cn: mouldable 加 -able：能够被塑成形状，就像湿陶土。

normal.en: British mould and American mold differ only in the u, just as colour and color do.
normal.cn: 英式与美式的差别只在那个 u，就像 colour 与 color 一样。

abstract.en: A mould is a promise made before the material arrives: the result is already written in the cavity.
abstract.cn: 模子是材料到来之前就许下的承诺：结果早已写在空腔里。

abstract.en: Shaping clay and shaping a child use one verb because both need gentle, repeated pressure.
abstract.cn: 塑造陶土与塑造孩子共用一个动词，因为两者都需要温和而反复的按压。

abstract.en: The fungus sense reminds us that damp, soft places quietly rewrite whatever rests in them.
abstract.cn: 表示霉的义项提醒人：潮湿柔软的地方会悄悄改写停放在那里的东西。

examples.en: She pressed the clay into a wooden mould and left it near the window to dry.
examples.cn: 她把陶土按进木模具，放在窗边晾干。

examples.en: There was grey mould along the bathroom tiles.
examples.cn: 浴室瓷砖的缝隙里长着灰霉。

examples.en: Years of reading moulded her into a patient observer.
examples.cn: 多年的阅读把她塑造成一个有耐心的观察者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「模得」——把湿泥按进框里，一脱模就得到一个形状；mould 既是模具，也是塑形。

root: 表示「成形」的 mould 来自拉丁语 modulus（小尺度，modus 的指小形式），经古法语 modle 进入英语；表示「霉」的义项一般认为另有来源，确切词源不确定；英式写 mould，美式写 mold。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a measured hollow that decides a shape; from it come the container, the pressing action and the shaping of a mind, while the fungus sense is a separate old word sharing the spelling.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个决定形状的量好空腔；由此分出容器、按压动作与心智的塑造，而表示霉的义项是共用拼写的另一个古词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: wet clay pressed into a wooden frame and turned out as a bowl.
core.cn: 核心意象：湿泥被按进木框，倒扣出来就是一只碗。

branches.en: rows of wooden frames waiting for clay
branches.cn: 一排等着装泥的木框

branches.en: a grey patch spreading over old bread
branches.cn: 旧面包上蔓延的灰斑

branches.en: a hand pressing wet sand into a castle
branches.cn: 一只手把湿沙压成城堡

branches.en: a teacher steadying a child's reading habit
branches.cn: 老师一点点扶正孩子的读书习惯

branches.en: a metal spoon lifted from a sand mould
branches.cn: 从砂模里取出的金属勺

intro.en: A Latin measure word, its diminutive, a French pattern word and English endings from -ing to -able hold the shaping family together; the fungus sense sits outside it.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语尺度词、它的指小形式、一个法语「样板」词，加上从 -ing 到 -able 的英语词尾，撑起了「成形」这一族；表示霉的义项在这一族之外。

latinIntro.en: Modus and its diminutive modulus belong to the Latin vocabulary of measuring; the fungus sense has no reliable Latin cognate and is left out of this list.
latinIntro.cn: modus 及其指小形式 modulus 属于拉丁语「量度」词汇；表示霉的义项没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因此不列入。

definition_zh: 登上；骑上；增加；安装；山
definition_en: to climb onto something such as a horse or a platform; to increase gradually; to fix something in position for use or display; a mountain, especially in names
core_image: 一个人抓着缰绳翻身上马，脚下石阶一级级往高处去
scene: 清晨的山道上，老人抓住缰绳，一脚踩稳马镫，翻身坐上马背。He mounted the grey horse and rode slowly up the stone path.
sceneCN: 这里「mount」是「登上、骑上」（第 1 个义项：爬上某物或骑上马背）；句意为他骑上那匹灰马，顺着石阶慢慢往山上走。画面里能想见：山道、缰绳、马镫与马背。

collocations.zh: 发起一场运动；开展一场活动

derivatives.zh: 由否定前缀 dis- 加 mount 构成，义为「下马；下车」
由前缀 re- 加 mount 构成，义为「重新骑上；重新安装」
由 mount 加 -ing 构成，义为「底座；装架；装裱材料」
由 mount 加 -able 构成，义为「可安装的；可骑上的」

senses.title: To climb onto a horse, bicycle or raised surface
senses.definition: to get onto a horse or bicycle, or to climb up onto a platform, wall or high place
senses.definitionCN: 上马或上车，或爬上一个台子、墙头或高处
senses.example: He mounted the grey horse and rode slowly up the stone path.
senses.exampleCN: 他骑上那匹灰马，顺着石阶慢慢往山上走。
senses.why: Mount comes from Latin mons, a mountain, through a verb that meant to go up; the first sense is simply upward movement onto something.
senses.whyCN: mount 经一个表示「往上走」的动词，来自拉丁语 mons（山）；第一个义项就是往上升、上到某物之上。

senses.title: To increase gradually, often until it becomes serious
senses.definition: to grow in amount, strength or intensity over time, especially in a way that causes concern
senses.definitionCN: 数量、力量或强度随时间增长，尤指增长到令人担忧的程度
senses.example: Pressure mounted on the committee as the deadline approached.
senses.exampleCN: 随着截止日期临近，委员会承受的压力越来越大。
senses.why: Going up is the core motion of the word, and a number or a feeling that goes up behaves like a climber gaining height.
senses.whyCN: 「往上走」是这个词的核心动作，而不断上升的数字或情绪，就像越爬越高的攀登者。

senses.title: To fix something in position for use or display
senses.definition: to attach an object firmly to a frame, wall or base so that it can be used, shown or studied
senses.definitionCN: 把某物牢固地装到框架、墙面或底座上，以便使用、展示或研究
senses.example: The technician mounted the camera above the entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 技术员把相机安装在入口上方。
senses.why: A thing placed up on a support is literally mounted, so the word keeps the upward picture while shifting from climbing to fixing in place.
senses.whyCN: 一件被放到支架上方的东西，字面上就是被 mount 上去，所以这个词从「爬上去」转为「固定住」时，仍保留着向上放置的画面。

senses.title: A mountain, especially in names and literary writing
senses.definition: a mountain or high hill, used mainly in proper names such as Mount Tai and in older or literary style
senses.definitionCN: 山或高山，主要用于泰山这类专名，以及较旧或文学性的文体中
senses.example: Snow still covered the upper slopes of the mount in early spring.
senses.exampleCN: 早春时，这座山的上部山坡仍覆着雪。
senses.why: The noun is the oldest layer of the word: Latin mons meant a mountain, and the name of the height stayed in English long after the verb took over everyday use.
senses.whyCN: 名词是这个词最古老的一层：拉丁语 mons 本义就是山，这一「高处之名」在动词接管日常用法之后很久仍留在英语里。

intro.en: Mount goes back to a Latin word for mountain, which also produced a verb meaning to climb; French carried both the height and the upward movement into English.
intro.cn: mount 可追到拉丁语表示「山」的词，同一个词又造出意为「攀登」的动词；法语把「高处」与「向上移动」这两层都带进了英语。

items.en: Mons meant a mountain or a high hill, and its stem mont- appears in mountain, amount and many place names.
items.cn: mons 意为山或高丘，其词干 mont- 出现在 mountain、amount 和许多地名中。

items.en: Everyday Latin built a verb montare from mons, meaning to go up or to climb; it is not recorded in formal texts but survives in the Romance languages.
items.cn: 民间拉丁语从 mons 造出动词 montare，意为往上走、攀登；它在正式文献中没有记录，却留在罗曼语族里。

items.en: Old French monter carried the senses of climbing, rising and getting on a horse, and it passed into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 monter 兼有攀登、上升与上马的意思，诺曼时期之后传入英语。

items.en: Middle English mounten covered climbing a hill, getting on horseback and rising in rank or value.
items.cn: 中古英语 mounten 涵盖爬山、上马，以及地位或价值的上升。

items.en: Modern English keeps the upward senses, adds fixing an object on a support, organizing a campaign, and the noun for a mountain used in names.
items.cn: 现代英语保留上升类义项，又添上把物件固定到支架上、组织一场运动，以及用于山名的名词义。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin mountain stem and its English family; the near-meaning group gathers words for climbing, rising and fixing in place.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语「山」词干及其英语词族展开；近义组收表示攀登、上升与固定安装的词。

entries.definition: A total or quantity, from the same Latin verb for going up.
entries.definitionCN: 总额或数量，来自同一个表示「往上升」的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: To get down off a horse or bicycle.
entries.definitionCN: 从马或自行车上下来。

entries.definition: To overcome a difficulty, or to stand on top of something.
entries.definitionCN: 克服困难，或位于某物之上。

entries.definition: A very high hill, built on the Latin mountain word.
entries.definitionCN: 很高的山，建立在拉丁语「山」这个词上。

entries.definition: A picture or film assembled from several pieces, from a French word for mounting.
entries.definitionCN: 把若干片段拼起来的画面或影片，源自法语中表示「装配」的词。

entries.definition: To go up something using hands and feet, or to rise steadily.
entries.definitionCN: 手脚并用地爬上某物，或稳定上升。

entries.definition: To move upwards, often in a steady or ceremonial way.
entries.definitionCN: 向上移动，常指平稳或庄重的上升。

entries.definition: To become larger in amount or degree.
entries.definitionCN: 数量或程度变大。

entries.definition: To fix equipment in place so that it can be used.
entries.definitionCN: 把设备安装到位以便使用。

normalIntro.en: The word climbs out of a Latin mountain word, and its family keeps returning to height, upward movement and things placed on a support.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从拉丁语表示「山」的词里爬出来，词族反复回到高度、向上的运动，以及被放到支架上的东西。

normal.en: Mons is Latin for mountain, so mount begins as a word about height and going up.
normal.cn: mons 是拉丁语的「山」，所以 mount 起初是一个关于高处与往上走的词。

normal.en: Old French monter gave English the verb, which is why mount and mountain look like relatives.
normal.cn: 古法语 monter 给了英语这个动词，所以 mount 与 mountain 看起来像亲戚。

normal.en: Dismount adds dis-: the reverse of getting on, therefore getting off.
normal.cn: dismount 加 dis-：与「上去」相反，因此是「下来」。

normal.en: Surmount adds sur- (above): to rise over an obstacle.
normal.cn: surmount 加 sur-（在上方）：升到障碍之上，即克服。

normal.en: 「Mounting costs」 are costs that keep climbing, and a picture mount is a support that holds the picture up.
normal.cn: 不断上升的成本像在往上爬，而画作的底座是把画托起来的东西。

abstract.en: Every sense of mount is a version of upward movement: a rider rises onto a horse, a number rises, a picture is lifted onto a wall.
abstract.cn: mount 的每个义项都是「向上」的一种版本：骑手升上马背，数字升高，画作被托上墙面。

abstract.en: A mountain is the most permanent thing one can mount, which is why the noun for height outlived the everyday verb.
abstract.cn: 山是人能登上的最持久的东西，所以表示高度的名词比日常动词活得更久。

abstract.en: Mounting a campaign is climbing in another form: gathering force until the effort stands above the noise.
abstract.cn: 发起一场运动是另一种形式的攀登：积蓄力量，直到这份努力高过周围的噪音。

examples.en: He mounted the grey horse and rode slowly up the stone path.
examples.cn: 他骑上那匹灰马，顺着石阶慢慢往山上走。

examples.en: Pressure mounted on the committee as the deadline approached.
examples.cn: 随着截止日期临近，委员会承受的压力越来越大。

examples.en: The technician mounted the camera above the entrance.
examples.cn: 技术员把相机安装在入口上方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「芒特」——登山的人喘着气喊出这个名字；mount 就是登上、攀升，也指山。

root: 拉丁语 mons（山，词干 mont-）在民间拉丁语中造出 montare（往上走、攀登），经古法语 monter 进入英语；同族词多与上升、山、安装有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is upward movement from and toward a height; the senses read it as climbing onto something, rising in degree, being placed on a support, and the height itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是朝高处、从高处发生的向上运动；义项把它读成爬上某物、程度上升、被放到支架上，以及高处本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rider gripping the reins and swinging up onto a horse, with stone steps climbing ahead.
core.cn: 核心意象：骑手抓住缰绳翻身上马，前面的石阶一级级往上。

branches.en: a rider lifting a boot into the stirrup
branches.cn: 骑手把靴子踏进马镫

branches.en: a pressure gauge needle creeping upward
branches.cn: 压力表指针一点点上移

branches.en: a camera raised and fixed above a door
branches.cn: 相机被举高并固定在门上方

branches.en: a picture lifted onto a gallery wall
branches.cn: 画作被托上画廊的墙

branches.en: a snow line drawn across a high ridge
branches.cn: 高脊上画出的雪线

intro.en: A Latin mountain word and its everyday verb, a French climbing verb and four English formations carry mount from a height to a motion, a support and a campaign.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语「山」词及其民间动词、一个法语攀登动词，加上四个英语构词形式，把 mount 从高处带到运动、支架与一场运动。

latinIntro.en: Mons, its accusative montem and the everyday verb montare are Latin forms behind the English family; montare appears only in informal usage.
latinIntro.cn: mons、它的宾格 montem 与民间动词 montare 是英语这一族词背后的拉丁词形；montare 只见于非正式用法。

items.meaning: to get off a horse or bicycle
